about: Every AArch64 instruction outside SVE and SME, with a plain-English description. The disassembler shows the entry for each instruction it prints. Refresh the forms with tools/arm-index.mjs; edit the text here.

source.forms: Arm A64 ISA XML for A-profile Architecture (developer.arm.com): mnemonics, form names, syntax templates, links
source.text: Descriptions written for this project; follow the links for the authoritative text

abs.description: Takes the absolute value of each element (or of a scalar) in a SIMD register. The most negative value stays unchanged instead of overflowing.

adc.description: Adds two registers plus the carry flag. Used to chain additions across multiple registers when computing numbers wider than 64 bits.

adcs.description: Like ADC but also updates the condition flags from the result. Used for the final or middle steps of multi-word additions that need overflow or carry info.
adcs.operation: Xd = Xn + Xm + C; NZCV = flags

add.description: Adds a register to another register (optionally shifted or extended) or to a small immediate. The everyday way to do integer addition and address arithmetic.

addg.description: Adds an immediate offset to an address and also changes its memory tag by a given amount. Part of the Memory Tagging Extension, used when tagging heap or stack allocations.

addhn.description: Adds two vectors of wide elements and keeps only the upper half of each sum, producing narrower elements in the lower half of the result.

addhn2.description: The "2" form of ADDHN: adds wide elements, keeps the high half of each sum, and writes them into the upper half of the destination, leaving the lower half unchanged.

addp.description: Adds adjacent pairs of elements taken from the two source vectors (or the two lanes of a vector for the scalar form). Handy for horizontal sums.

addpt.description: Adds an offset to a pointer using checked-pointer arithmetic from the Checked Pointer Arithmetic extension, leaving the upper pointer-protection bits consistent.

adds.description: Adds like ADD but also updates the N, Z, C and V flags. Used when the result is tested for zero, negative or overflow; CMN is an alias with the result discarded.

addv.description: Sums all lanes of a vector into one scalar value. Typically emitted for reductions such as summing an array of integers.

adr.description: Computes an address relative to the current instruction, within about plus or minus 1 MB. Used to reference nearby labels or data.

adrp.description: Computes the 4 KB page address of a label relative to the PC, giving a range of plus or minus 4 GB. Usually paired with an ADD or a load to reach a global variable.

aesd.description: Performs one AES decryption step (inverse ShiftRows and SubBytes after XORing the round key) on a 128-bit block.

aese.description: Performs one AES encryption step (XOR with the round key, then ShiftRows and SubBytes) on a 128-bit block.

aesimc.description: Applies the AES InvMixColumns transform to a 128-bit block, used when preparing decryption round keys and in decryption rounds.

aesmc.description: Applies the AES MixColumns transform to a 128-bit block, completing an encryption round after AESE.

and.description: Computes the bitwise AND of a register with another register (optionally shifted) or a bitmask immediate. Used to mask bits or clear fields.

ands.description: ANDs two values and sets N and Z from the result, clearing C and V. TST is an alias that discards the result.

apas.description: Memory-tagging maintenance instruction (Realm/Granule Protection) that changes the physical address space associated with a tag for an address.

asr.description: An alias of ASRV (register shift) or SBFM (immediate shift). Shifts right while copying the sign bit in, so signed values keep their sign.

asrv.description: Shifts a register right by an amount held in another register, filling with the sign bit. The shift amount is taken modulo the register size.

at.description: An alias of SYS that asks the MMU to translate a virtual address and report the result in PAR_EL1. Used by operating systems and hypervisors.

autda.description: Checks the pointer authentication code on a data pointer using key A and a modifier register. On success the code is removed; on failure the pointer is made invalid.

autdb.description: Verifies and strips the pointer authentication code of a data pointer using key B and a register modifier. A bad signature yields a non-canonical pointer.

autdza.description: Like AUTDA but with a modifier of zero. Verifies and strips the signature of a data pointer signed with key A.

autdzb.description: Like AUTDB but with a modifier of zero. Verifies and strips the signature of a data pointer signed with key B.

autia.description: Verifies and strips the pointer authentication code on a code pointer using instruction key A and a modifier register. Often seen before returns or indirect calls.

autia1716.description: Hint-space form that authenticates the code pointer in X17 using key A with X16 as modifier. Used in PLT stubs.

autia171615.description: Variant that authenticates X17 using key A with X16 as the modifier and X15 as additional context, as used in the PAuth_LR scheme.

autiasp.description: Authenticates the return address in X30 using key A with the stack pointer as modifier. Compilers put it in function epilogues to catch corrupted return addresses.

autiasppc.description: Authenticates the link register using key A with a modifier derived from the PC and a label offset, part of the PAuth_LR extension.

autiasppcr.description: PAuth_LR form that authenticates a register holding a return address using key A and a PC-based modifier.

autiaz.description: Authenticates the link register X30 using key A with a zero modifier.

autib.description: Verifies and strips the pointer authentication code on a code pointer using instruction key B and a register modifier.

autib1716.description: Hint-space form that authenticates X17 using key B with X16 as modifier.

autib171615.description: Authenticates X17 using key B with X16 as modifier and X15 as extra context, from the PAuth_LR extension.

autibsp.description: Authenticates the return address in X30 using key B and the stack pointer as modifier. Common in function epilogues when B-key signing is enabled.

autibsppc.description: Authenticates the link register using key B with a modifier derived from the PC and a label offset (PAuth_LR).

autibsppcr.description: PAuth_LR form that authenticates a register holding a return address using key B and a PC-based modifier.

autibz.description: Authenticates the link register X30 using key B with a zero modifier.

autiza.description: Like AUTIA but with a zero modifier: verifies and strips the signature of a code pointer signed with key A.

autizb.description: Like AUTIB but with a zero modifier: verifies and strips the signature of a code pointer signed with key B.

axflag.summary: Convert FP flags to alternative format
axflag.description: Converts floating-point comparison flags from the Arm form into an alternative encoding (the inverse of XAFLAG). Helps emulate other architectures conventions.

b.description: Unconditional jump to a PC-relative label (range about plus or minus 128 MB). Used for loops, goto and tail calls.

b.cond.description: Jumps to a label only if a condition holds. The condition is a suffix (b.eq, b.ne, b.lt, b.ge, b.hi ...) that tests the NZCV flags set by an earlier compare or flag-setting instruction.

bc.cond.description: Conditional branch (same condition suffixes as b.cond, e.g. bc.eq) with a hint that the outcome is consistent and highly predictable. Tests the NZCV flags.

bcax.description: Three-way operation: clears from Vn the bits that are set in Vm, then XORs with Va. Speeds up SHA-3 style algorithms.

bf1cvtl.description: Widens the lower half of a vector of 8-bit floating-point (FP8, E5M2 variant) values to half-precision values.

bf1cvtl2.description: The "2" form: widens the upper half of the source FP8 (E5M2 variant) vector to half-precision elements.

bf2cvtl.description: Widens the lower half of a vector of 8-bit floating-point (FP8, E4M3 variant) values to half-precision values.

bf2cvtl2.description: The "2" form: widens the upper half of the source FP8 (E4M3 variant) vector to half-precision elements.

bfc.description: An alias of BFM that clears a run of bits in a register to zero while leaving the others untouched.

bfcvt.description: Converts a single-precision float to the 16-bit bfloat16 format (same exponent range, fewer mantissa bits). Common in machine-learning code.

bfcvtn.description: Narrows a vector of single-precision floats to bfloat16 values, placing them in the lower half of the destination.

bfcvtn2.description: The "2" form of BFCVTN: narrows floats to bfloat16 and writes them into the upper half of the destination.

bfdot.description: Multiplies pairs of bfloat16 values from two vectors and adds both products into each single-precision accumulator lane.

bfi.description: An alias of BFM that copies the low bits of a source register into a chosen position of the destination, leaving other bits alone.

bfm.description: General bitfield copy that moves a field from one register into another, keeping other destination bits. BFI, BFXIL and BFC are aliases.

bfmlal.description: Multiplies bfloat16 elements and accumulates the single-precision products into the destination. The B (bottom) and T (top) forms select even or odd source lanes.

bfmlalb.description: Takes the bfloat16 values in the even-numbered halfword lanes, multiplies them and adds the products to the single-precision lanes of the destination. The by-element form uses one bfloat16 value for every lane.

bfmlalt.description: Takes the bfloat16 values in the odd-numbered halfword lanes, multiplies them and adds the products to the single-precision lanes of the destination. Paired with bfmlalb it covers all eight lanes.

bfmmla.description: Treats the sources as small bfloat16 matrices, multiplies them and adds the result into a 2x2 single-precision matrix. Used for ML kernels.

bfxil.description: An alias of BFM that takes a field from a source register and inserts it into the lowest bits of the destination.

bic.description: Clears the bits in the first operand that are set in the second (AND with the inverse). Has register and SIMD immediate forms.

bics.description: Does a bit clear (AND NOT) and updates N and Z from the result, clearing C and V.

bif.description: Copies bits from the first source into the destination only where the mask register has zero bits.

bit.description: Copies bits from the first source into the destination only where the mask register has one bits.

bl.description: Calls a function: saves the return address in X30 (LR) and jumps to a PC-relative label. The standard direct function call.

blr.description: Calls a function through an address in a register, saving the return address in X30. Used for function pointers and virtual calls.

blraa.description: Authenticates a code pointer with instruction key A and a register modifier, then calls it, saving the return address in X30.

blraaz.description: Authenticates the pointer in a register with key A and a zero modifier, then calls it.

blrab.description: Authenticates a code pointer with instruction key B and a register modifier, then calls it.

blrabz.description: Authenticates the pointer in a register with key B and a zero modifier, then calls it.

br.description: Jumps to the address held in a register without saving a return address. Used for switch tables and indirect tail calls.

braa.description: Authenticates a code pointer using key A and a register modifier, then jumps to it.

braaz.description: Authenticates the pointer with key A and a zero modifier, then jumps to it.

brab.description: Authenticates a code pointer using key B and a register modifier, then jumps to it.

brabz.description: Authenticates the pointer with key B and a zero modifier, then jumps to it.

brb.description: An alias of SYS used to invalidate the Branch Record Buffer, a hardware log of recent branches used for profiling.

brk.description: Raises a software breakpoint exception, which usually stops execution in a debugger. Compilers emit it for traps such as unreachable code.

bsl.description: Uses the destination as a mask: picks bits from the first source where the mask is 1 and from the second where it is 0. A SIMD ternary select.

bti.description: Marks a legal landing spot for indirect branches. With BTI enabled, jumping elsewhere with BR or BLR faults, hardening against ROP/JOP attacks. Acts as a NOP on older CPUs.

cas.description: Atomically compares a 32- or 64-bit value in memory with an expected value and, if equal, stores a new value; the old value is returned in the first register. Memory ordering: relaxed. Basis of lock-free algorithms.
cas.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Xs) [Xn] = Xt; Xs = old

casa.description: Atomically compares a 32- or 64-bit value in memory with an expected value and, if equal, stores a new value; the old value is returned in the first register. Memory ordering: acquire. Basis of lock-free algorithms.
casa.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Xs) [Xn] = Xt; Xs = old

casab.description: Atomically compares a byte in memory with an expected value and, if equal, stores a new value; the old value is returned in the first register. Memory ordering: acquire. Basis of lock-free algorithms.
casab.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Ws) [Xn] = Wt; Ws = old

casah.description: Atomically compares a halfword in memory with an expected value and, if equal, stores a new value; the old value is returned in the first register. Memory ordering: acquire. Basis of lock-free algorithms.
casah.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Ws) [Xn] = Wt; Ws = old

casal.description: Atomically compares a 32- or 64-bit value in memory with an expected value and, if equal, stores a new value; the old value is returned in the first register. Memory ordering: acquire-release. Basis of lock-free algorithms.
casal.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Xs) [Xn] = Xt; Xs = old

casalb.description: Atomically compares a byte in memory with an expected value and, if equal, stores a new value; the old value is returned in the first register. Memory ordering: acquire-release. Basis of lock-free algorithms.
casalb.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Ws) [Xn] = Wt; Ws = old

casalh.description: Atomically compares a halfword in memory with an expected value and, if equal, stores a new value; the old value is returned in the first register. Memory ordering: acquire-release. Basis of lock-free algorithms.
casalh.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Ws) [Xn] = Wt; Ws = old

casalt.description: Compare-and-swap that checks memory as if executed at EL0 (unprivileged), from the LSUI extension. Lets kernels do atomic updates on user memory. Ordering: acquire-release.
casalt.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Xs) [Xn] = Xt; Xs = old

casat.description: Compare-and-swap that checks memory as if executed at EL0 (unprivileged), from the LSUI extension. Lets kernels do atomic updates on user memory. Ordering: acquire.
casat.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Xs) [Xn] = Xt; Xs = old

casb.description: Atomically compares a byte in memory with an expected value and, if equal, stores a new value; the old value is returned in the first register. Memory ordering: relaxed. Basis of lock-free algorithms.
casb.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Ws) [Xn] = Wt; Ws = old

cash.description: Atomically compares a halfword in memory with an expected value and, if equal, stores a new value; the old value is returned in the first register. Memory ordering: relaxed. Basis of lock-free algorithms.
cash.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Ws) [Xn] = Wt; Ws = old

casl.description: Atomically compares a 32- or 64-bit value in memory with an expected value and, if equal, stores a new value; the old value is returned in the first register. Memory ordering: release. Basis of lock-free algorithms.
casl.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Xs) [Xn] = Xt; Xs = old

caslb.description: Atomically compares a byte in memory with an expected value and, if equal, stores a new value; the old value is returned in the first register. Memory ordering: release. Basis of lock-free algorithms.
caslb.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Ws) [Xn] = Wt; Ws = old

caslh.description: Atomically compares a halfword in memory with an expected value and, if equal, stores a new value; the old value is returned in the first register. Memory ordering: release. Basis of lock-free algorithms.
caslh.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Ws) [Xn] = Wt; Ws = old

caslt.description: Compare-and-swap that checks memory as if executed at EL0 (unprivileged), from the LSUI extension. Lets kernels do atomic updates on user memory. Ordering: release.
caslt.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Xs) [Xn] = Xt; Xs = old

casp.description: Atomically compares a pair of adjacent registers with a 2x-wide memory location and, if equal, stores a new pair. Ordering: relaxed. Used for double-width lock-free updates such as pointer plus counter.
casp.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Xs:Xs+1) [Xn] = Xt:Xt+1; Xs:Xs+1 = old

caspa.description: Atomically compares a pair of adjacent registers with a 2x-wide memory location and, if equal, stores a new pair. Ordering: acquire. Used for double-width lock-free updates such as pointer plus counter.
caspa.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Xs:Xs+1) [Xn] = Xt:Xt+1; Xs:Xs+1 = old

caspal.description: Atomically compares a pair of adjacent registers with a 2x-wide memory location and, if equal, stores a new pair. Ordering: acquire-release. Used for double-width lock-free updates such as pointer plus counter.
caspal.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Xs:Xs+1) [Xn] = Xt:Xt+1; Xs:Xs+1 = old

caspalt.description: Pair compare-and-swap performed with unprivileged (EL0) access permissions, from the LSUI extension. Ordering: acquire-release.
caspalt.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Xs:Xs+1) [Xn] = Xt:Xt+1; Xs:Xs+1 = old

caspat.description: Pair compare-and-swap performed with unprivileged (EL0) access permissions, from the LSUI extension. Ordering: acquire.
caspat.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Xs:Xs+1) [Xn] = Xt:Xt+1; Xs:Xs+1 = old

caspl.description: Atomically compares a pair of adjacent registers with a 2x-wide memory location and, if equal, stores a new pair. Ordering: release. Used for double-width lock-free updates such as pointer plus counter.
caspl.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Xs:Xs+1) [Xn] = Xt:Xt+1; Xs:Xs+1 = old

casplt.description: Pair compare-and-swap performed with unprivileged (EL0) access permissions, from the LSUI extension. Ordering: release.
casplt.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Xs:Xs+1) [Xn] = Xt:Xt+1; Xs:Xs+1 = old

caspt.description: Pair compare-and-swap performed with unprivileged (EL0) access permissions, from the LSUI extension. Ordering: relaxed.
caspt.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Xs:Xs+1) [Xn] = Xt:Xt+1; Xs:Xs+1 = old

cast.description: Compare-and-swap that checks memory as if executed at EL0 (unprivileged), from the LSUI extension. Lets kernels do atomic updates on user memory. Ordering: relaxed.
cast.operation: old = [Xn]; if (old == Xs) [Xn] = Xt; Xs = old

cbbeq.description: Compares the low byte of two registers and branches to a label in one instruction if the result is equal. Fuses a compare and conditional branch without touching the flags (FEAT_CMPBR).

cbbge.summary: Compare and branch if signed greater or equal (byte)
cbbge.description: Compares the low byte of two registers and branches to a label in one instruction if the result is signed greater or equal. Fuses a compare and conditional branch without touching the flags (FEAT_CMPBR).

cbbgt.summary: Compare and branch if signed greater than (byte)
cbbgt.description: Compares the low byte of two registers and branches to a label in one instruction if the result is signed greater than. Fuses a compare and conditional branch without touching the flags (FEAT_CMPBR).

cbbhi.summary: Compare and branch if unsigned higher (byte)
cbbhi.description: Compares the low byte of two registers and branches to a label in one instruction if the result is unsigned higher. Fuses a compare and conditional branch without touching the flags (FEAT_CMPBR).

cbne.description: Compares a register with another register or an immediate and branches to a label in one instruction if the result is not equal. Fuses a compare and conditional branch without touching the flags (FEAT_CMPBR).

cbnz.description: Branches to a label if a register is not zero, without altering flags. Typical for loop counters and null checks.

cbz.description: Branches to a label if a register is zero, without altering flags. Typical for null-pointer checks and loop exits.

ccmn.description: If the condition holds, compares a register with the negation of a value (like CMN); otherwise sets the flags to a given constant. Used to chain && and || conditions.
ccmn.operation: if (cond) flags = Xn + op2 else NZCV = #nzcv

ccmp.description: If the condition holds, compares two values like CMP; otherwise sets the flags to a given constant. Lets compilers combine several comparisons without branches.
ccmp.operation: if (cond) flags = Xn - op2 else NZCV = #nzcv

cfinv.description: Flips the carry flag C, leaving N, Z and V unchanged. Used when converting between borrow and carry conventions.

cfp.description: An alias of SYS that restricts speculative control-flow predictions for a given context, used as a Spectre mitigation.

chkfeat.description: Hint that reports whether a given architectural feature (such as guarded control stacks) is enabled, by clearing the matching bit of X16.

cinc.description: An alias of CSINC: returns Xn + 1 if the condition is true, otherwise Xn. Handy for turning comparisons into counts.

cinv.description: An alias of CSINV: returns the bitwise NOT of Xn if the condition is true, otherwise Xn.

clrbhb.description: Hint that clears the branch history buffer so earlier code cannot influence later branch prediction, a Spectre-BHB mitigation.

clrex.description: Clears the local exclusive-access monitor so a pending load-exclusive/store-exclusive pair will fail. Used on context switches or exception returns.

cls.description: Counts how many bits after the top bit match the sign bit. Useful for normalising signed numbers.

clz.description: Counts the zero bits from the top until the first 1. Used for log2, bit scanning and normalisation.

cmeq.description: Compares each element for equality (or with zero) and writes all ones to a lane if true, all zeros if false. Result masks feed bit-select operations.

cmge.description: Per-lane compare of two vectors; each result lane becomes all ones if the test (signed >=) holds, otherwise all zeros. Used by vectorised code to build masks for selects or counting.

cmgt.description: Per-lane compare of two vectors; each result lane becomes all ones if the test (signed >) holds, otherwise all zeros. Used by vectorised code to build masks for selects or counting.

cmhi.description: Per-lane compare of two vectors; each result lane becomes all ones if the test (unsigned >) holds, otherwise all zeros. Used by vectorised code to build masks for selects or counting.

cmhs.description: Per-lane compare of two vectors; each result lane becomes all ones if the test (unsigned >=) holds, otherwise all zeros. Used by vectorised code to build masks for selects or counting.

cmle.description: Per-lane compare of each element with zero; each result lane becomes all ones if the test (signed <= 0) holds, otherwise all zeros. Used by vectorised code to build masks for selects or counting.

cmlt.description: Per-lane compare of each element with zero; each result lane becomes all ones if the test (signed < 0) holds, otherwise all zeros. Used by vectorised code to build masks for selects or counting.

cmn.description: An alias of ADDS with the result thrown away: it adds two operands only to set the condition flags. Handy for testing against a negative constant, e.g. x == -imm.

cmp.description: An alias of SUBS with the result discarded: it subtracts the second operand from the first just to set the condition flags. Emitted before conditional branches and selects.

cmpp.description: An alias of SUBPS with the result discarded. Compares two pointers by their address bits (ignoring memory tags) and sets the flags.

cmtst.description: Per-lane test: a result lane is all ones if the two source elements share at least one set bit, else zero.

cneg.description: An alias of CSNEG. Gives the negated source if the condition is true, otherwise the unchanged source. Often used for branch-free absolute value.

cnt.description: Counts the 1 bits in each byte lane of the vector. The usual building block for a population count (popcount), followed by a horizontal add.

cosp.description: An alias of SYS that restricts speculative use of cached prediction state (COSP RCTX) for the given context. Used by security mitigations against speculation attacks.

cpp.description: An alias of SYS that invalidates branch/prediction state tied to a context (CPP RCTX), used as a speculation-attack mitigation.

crc32b.description: Folds one byte of data into a running CRC-32 (IEEE polynomial) value. Used in checksums and hashing.

crc32cb.description: Folds one byte into a running CRC-32C (Castagnoli polynomial) value, as used by iSCSI, ext4 and others.

crc32ch.description: Folds a 16-bit value into a running CRC-32C (Castagnoli polynomial).

crc32cw.description: Folds a 32-bit value into a running CRC-32C (Castagnoli polynomial).

crc32cx.description: Folds a 64-bit value into a running CRC-32C (Castagnoli polynomial).

crc32h.description: Folds a 16-bit value into a running CRC-32 (IEEE polynomial).

crc32w.description: Folds a 32-bit value into a running CRC-32 (IEEE polynomial).

crc32x.description: Folds a 64-bit value into a running CRC-32 (IEEE polynomial).

csdb.description: A hint that stops later instructions from using speculatively produced data values. Part of Spectre-style mitigations; harmless NOP on cores that do not need it.

csel.description: Picks the first source if the condition holds, otherwise the second. The standard branch-free way to write a ternary like c ? a : b.

cset.description: An alias of CSINC. Sets the register to 1 if the condition is true, else 0. Typically turns a comparison into a bool.

csetm.description: An alias of CSINV. Sets the register to all ones (-1) if the condition is true, else 0. Produces a full mask from a comparison.

csinc.description: Picks the first source if the condition holds, otherwise the second source plus one. Also underlies CSET and CINC.

csinv.description: Picks the first source if the condition holds, otherwise the bitwise NOT of the second. Underlies CSETM and CINV.

csneg.description: Picks the first source if the condition holds, otherwise the negation of the second. Underlies CNEG; used for abs() and sign handling.

ctz.description: Counts how many zero bits sit at the low end of the register (the index of the lowest set bit); gives the register width if the value is zero.

dc.description: An alias of SYS for data cache maintenance by address or set/way (e.g. DC CIVAC, DC ZVA): clean, invalidate or zero cache lines. Used by drivers, JITs and memory allocators.

dcps1.summary: Debug change PE state to EL1
dcps1.description: Debug-state instruction that switches execution to exception level 1. Only usable while in Debug state.

dcps2.summary: Debug change PE state to EL2
dcps2.description: Debug-state instruction that switches execution to exception level 2. Only usable while in Debug state.

dcps3.summary: Debug change PE state to EL3
dcps3.description: Debug-state instruction that switches execution to exception level 3. Only usable while in Debug state.

dfb.description: The name LLVM gives DSB with option 12, a barrier defined by the Armv8-R AArch64 profile for real-time processors. On the A-profile processors of phones and Macs the option is reserved.

dgh.description: A hint telling the CPU that earlier memory accesses may be combined (gathered) with later ones. A NOP where unsupported.

dmb.description: Makes sure earlier memory accesses of the stated kind are observed before later ones. Used to order memory in lock-free and multi-threaded code.

drps.description: Debug-state return instruction that restores processor state from the saved debug registers. Rarely seen outside debuggers.

dsb.description: Stronger than DMB: waits until all earlier memory accesses (and cache/TLB maintenance) have fully completed before continuing.

dup.description: Copies one element, or a general-purpose register, into every lane of a vector (or into a scalar). Used to splat a constant or scalar across a vector.

dvp.description: An alias of SYS that restricts data value prediction for a context (DVP RCTX), used in speculation-attack mitigations.

eon.description: XORs the first register with the bitwise inverse of the (optionally shifted) second.

eor.description: XORs two registers, or a register and a bitmask immediate. Common for toggling bits and, with itself, zeroing a register.

eor3.description: XORs three vectors together in one instruction. Speeds up crypto routines such as SHA-3.

eret.description: Returns from an exception handler: restores PC from ELR and PSTATE from SPSR, dropping to the previous exception level. Kernel/hypervisor use only.

eretaa.description: Like ERET but first authenticates the return address in ELR using key A (with SP as modifier); traps/faults on failure.

eretab.description: Like ERET but first authenticates the return address in ELR using key B (with SP as modifier); faults on failure.

esb.description: Hint that forces pending asynchronous errors (RAS) to be recorded before continuing. NOP on cores without that feature.

ext.description: Takes bytes from the concatenation of two vectors starting at a byte offset. Used to shift/rotate a vector by whole elements, e.g. sliding windows.

extr.description: Takes a register-width window out of two concatenated registers starting at a bit position. With both sources equal it is a rotate right (ROR).

f1cvtl.description: Widens the lower half of a vector of 8-bit floating-point values (format 1) to half precision.

f1cvtl2.description: Like F1CVTL but reads the upper half of the 8-bit source vector.

f2cvtl.description: Widens the lower half of a vector of 8-bit floating-point values (format 2) to half precision.

f2cvtl2.description: Like F2CVTL but reads the upper half of the 8-bit source vector.

fabd.description: Computes the absolute value of the difference between two floating-point numbers. Works on scalars or per lane on vectors.

fabs.description: Clears the sign of a floating-point value, giving its magnitude. Used for fabs()/abs() on floats.

facge.summary: FP absolute compare greater or equal
facge.description: Compares the magnitudes of two floats and yields an all-ones mask in each lane where |n| >= |m|, else zero.

facgt.description: Compares magnitudes of two floats per lane; the lane becomes all-ones where |n| > |m|, otherwise zero.

fadd.description: Adds two floating-point values, either scalar or lane by lane in a vector.

faddp.description: Adds adjacent pairs of floats. The scalar form sums the two elements of one vector; the vector form pairs up elements from both sources.
faddp.operation: Vd = pairwise sum of adjacent elements

famax.description: Per lane, picks whichever operand has the larger magnitude and keeps its absolute value. Part of the FAMINMAX extension.

famin.description: Per lane, picks whichever operand has the smaller magnitude and keeps its absolute value. Part of the FAMINMAX extension.

fcadd.description: Adds complex numbers stored as (real, imaginary) pairs, after rotating the second operand by 90 or 270 degrees. Helps complex-number arithmetic.

fccmp.description: If the condition holds, compares two floats and sets the flags from the result; otherwise sets the flags to an immediate value. Used to chain float comparisons in && / || expressions.

fccmpe.description: Like FCCMP but also raises an invalid-operation exception if either operand is any NaN, including quiet NaNs.

fcmeq.description: Compares floats for equality, giving an all-ones mask where equal and zero otherwise. Can compare against zero.

fcmge.description: Per lane, sets the result to all-ones if the first float is >= the second (or >= 0), else zero.

fcmgt.description: Per lane, sets the result to all-ones if the first float is > the second (or > 0), else zero.

fcmla.description: Multiplies-accumulates complex numbers held as (real, imaginary) pairs with a chosen rotation (0, 90, 180, 270). Two instructions with different rotations make a full complex multiply.

fcmle.summary: FP compare less or equal to zero
fcmle.description: Per lane, gives all-ones if the float is <= 0.0, otherwise zero.

fcmlt.description: Per lane, gives all-ones if the float is < 0.0, otherwise zero.

fcmp.description: Compares two floats (or one against zero) and writes the result to the condition flags, for a following conditional branch or select. Unordered (NaN) sets C and V.

fcmpe.description: Like FCMP but raises an invalid-operation exception for any NaN operand, even a quiet one. Compilers use it for ordered comparisons such as < and >.
fcmpe.operation: NZCV = compare(Vn, Vm), trap on NaN

fcsel.description: Chooses one of two floating-point registers depending on a condition code, like a ternary operator on floats.

fcvt.description: Converts a float between half, single and double precision (and BFloat16/FP8 in newer cores).

fcvtas.summary: FP to signed int, round to nearest away
fcvtas.description: Converts a float to a signed integer, rounding to nearest with ties going away from zero.

fcvtau.summary: FP to unsigned int, round to nearest away
fcvtau.description: Converts a float to an unsigned integer, rounding to nearest with ties away from zero.

fcvtl.description: Widens each float in the lower half of the source vector to the next larger precision (e.g. 2 singles to 2 doubles).

fcvtl2.description: Same as FCVTL but widens the upper half of the source vector.

fcvtms.summary: FP to signed int, round toward -inf
fcvtms.description: Converts a float to a signed integer, rounding down (floor).

fcvtmu.summary: FP to unsigned int, round toward -inf
fcvtmu.description: Converts a float to an unsigned integer, rounding down (floor).

fcvtn.description: Narrows each float to the next smaller precision (e.g. doubles to singles), writing the lower half of the destination and zeroing the upper half.

forms.heading: FCVTN, FCVTN2 (double to single-precision, single to half-precision)

fcvtn2.description: Like FCVTN but writes the narrowed results into the upper half of the destination, leaving the lower half unchanged.

forms.heading: FCVTN, FCVTN2 (double to single-precision, single to half-precision)

fcvtns.summary: FP to signed int, round to nearest even
fcvtns.description: Converts a float to a signed integer, rounding to nearest with ties to even.

fcvtnu.summary: FP to unsigned int, round to nearest even
fcvtnu.description: Converts a float to an unsigned integer, rounding to nearest with ties to even.

fcvtps.summary: FP to signed int, round toward +inf
fcvtps.description: Converts a float to a signed integer, rounding up (ceil).

fcvtpu.summary: FP to unsigned int, round toward +inf
fcvtpu.description: Converts a float to an unsigned integer, rounding up (ceil).

fcvtxn.summary: FP narrow with round to odd
fcvtxn.description: Narrows doubles to singles using round-to-odd, which avoids double-rounding errors when a later step rounds again.

fcvtxn2.description: Like FCVTXN but writes the narrowed results to the upper half of the destination.

fcvtzs.summary: FP to signed int, round toward zero
fcvtzs.description: Converts a float to a signed integer by truncating, which is what a C cast (int)x does. Can also convert to fixed-point.

fcvtzu.summary: FP to unsigned int, round toward zero
fcvtzu.description: Converts a float to an unsigned integer by truncating, like a C cast to unsigned. Can also produce fixed-point.

fdiv.description: Divides one float by another, scalar or per vector lane.

fdot.description: Multiplies pairs (or groups of four for 8-bit) of small floats and adds the sums into wider accumulators. Used for machine-learning kernels.

forms.heading: FDOT (8-bit floating-point to half-precision, by element)
FDOT (8-bit floating-point to single-precision, by element)

fjcvtzs.description: Converts a double to a signed 32-bit integer using JavaScript semantics (truncate, wrap modulo 2^32). Used by JS engines for the ToInt32 operation.

fmadd.description: Computes a*b + c with a single rounding. Compilers emit it for a*b+c and fma().

fmax.description: Returns the larger of two floats; if either is a NaN the result is NaN.

fmaxnm.description: Returns the larger of two floats but prefers a number over a quiet NaN, like C fmax().

fmaxnmp.description: Takes the maximum of adjacent element pairs, preferring numbers over quiet NaNs.
fmaxnmp.operation: Vd = pairwise fmax of adjacent elements

fmaxnmv.description: Reduces all lanes of a vector to a single maximum, preferring numbers over quiet NaNs.
fmaxnmv.operation: Sd = fmax over all Vn lanes

fmaxp.description: Takes the maximum of adjacent element pairs; NaNs propagate.
fmaxp.operation: Vd = pairwise max of adjacent elements

fmaxv.description: Reduces all lanes of a vector to the single largest float; NaNs propagate.
fmaxv.operation: Sd = max over all Vn lanes

fmin.description: Returns the smaller of two floats; if either is a NaN the result is NaN.

fminnm.description: Returns the smaller of two floats but prefers a number over a quiet NaN, like C fmin().

fminnmp.description: Takes the minimum of adjacent element pairs, preferring numbers over quiet NaNs.
fminnmp.operation: Vd = pairwise fmin of adjacent elements

fminnmv.description: Reduces all lanes of a vector to a single minimum, preferring numbers over quiet NaNs.
fminnmv.operation: Sd = fmin over all Vn lanes

fminp.description: Takes the minimum of adjacent element pairs; NaNs propagate.
fminp.operation: Vd = pairwise min of adjacent elements

fminv.description: Reduces all lanes of a vector to the single smallest float; NaNs propagate.
fminv.operation: Sd = min over all Vn lanes

fmla.description: Multiplies two vectors (or a vector by one element) and adds the products into the destination, fused with one rounding.

fmlal.description: Multiplies half-precision values from the lower half of the sources and accumulates into single-precision lanes.

fmlal2.description: Like FMLAL but takes the half-precision inputs from the upper half of the source vectors.

fmlalb.description: Multiplies 8-bit floats from even-numbered byte lanes and accumulates into half-precision lanes. Used for low-precision ML.

fmlallbb.description: Multiplies 8-bit floats (bottom-selected from both sources) and accumulates into single-precision lanes.

fmlallbt.description: Multiplies 8-bit floats (bottom from first, top from second source) and accumulates into single-precision lanes.

fmlalltb.description: Multiplies 8-bit floats (top from first, bottom from second source) and accumulates into single-precision lanes.

fmlalltt.description: Multiplies 8-bit floats taken from the top positions of both sources and accumulates into single-precision lanes.

fmlalt.description: Multiplies 8-bit floats from odd-numbered byte lanes and accumulates into half-precision lanes.

fmls.description: Multiplies two vectors (or a vector by an element) and subtracts the products from the destination, fused with one rounding.

fmlsl.description: Multiplies half-precision values from the lower halves and subtracts the products from single-precision accumulators.

fmlsl2.description: Like FMLSL but uses the upper halves of the half-precision source vectors.

fmmla.description: Treats vector segments as small matrices, multiplies them, and adds the result to the accumulator. Accelerates matrix math and ML.

fmov.description: Copies a float register, loads a small encodable constant, or moves raw bits between general and FP/SIMD registers without converting.

fmsub.description: Computes c - a*b with a single rounding.

fmul.description: Multiplies two floats, scalar, per lane, or by a vector element.

fmulx.description: Like FMUL but returns 2.0 (with the right sign) for 0 times infinity instead of NaN. Used in reciprocal-estimate sequences.

fneg.description: Flips the sign of a float.

fnmadd.description: Computes -(a*b) - c with a single rounding.

fnmsub.description: Computes a*b - c with a single rounding.

fnmul.description: Multiplies two floats and negates the product.

frecpe.description: Gives a rough (about 8-bit accurate) estimate of 1/x, to be refined with FRECPS Newton-Raphson steps.

frecps.description: Computes 2 - a*b, a helper used to refine a reciprocal estimate by Newton-Raphson iteration.

frecpx.description: Produces a value from the exponent of the input (roughly inverts the exponent, zeroes the fraction). Used when scaling in division sequences.
frecpx.operation: Vd = approx exponent inverse of Vn

frint32x.description: Rounds a float to an integral value that fits in 32 bits using the current rounding mode, raising Inexact if it changed.

frint32z.description: Rounds a float toward zero to an integral value in the 32-bit range.

frint64x.description: Rounds a float to an integral value that fits in 64 bits using the current rounding mode, raising Inexact if it changed.

frint64z.description: Rounds a float toward zero to an integral value in the 64-bit range.

frinta.description: Rounds a float to a whole number, ties away from zero, like C round().

frinti.description: Rounds a float to a whole number using the current rounding mode, like nearbyint().

frintm.description: Rounds a float down to a whole number, like floor().

frintn.description: Rounds a float to the nearest whole number, ties to even, like roundeven().

frintp.description: Rounds a float up to a whole number, like ceil().

frintx.description: Rounds a float to a whole number with the current rounding mode and raises Inexact if the value changed, like rint().

frintz.description: Truncates a float to a whole number, like trunc().

frsqrte.description: Gives a rough estimate of 1/sqrt(x), refined with FRSQRTS steps.

frsqrts.description: Computes (3 - a*b)/2, a helper for Newton-Raphson refinement of a reciprocal square root.

fscale.summary: FP scale by power of two
fscale.description: Multiplies each float by 2 raised to an integer taken from the second operand, like ldexp().

fsqrt.description: Computes the square root of a float.

fsub.description: Subtracts one float from another, scalar or per lane.

gcsb.description: Barrier that makes earlier guarded-control-stack updates complete before later ones. The only operand is DSYNC.

gcspopcx.summary: GCS pop and compare exception state
gcspopcx.description: Pops an exception-return record from the guarded control stack and checks it against the current state; used by exception handling code.

gcspopm.description: Pops the top entry from the guarded control stack, optionally returning the value in a register. Used by unwinders such as longjmp.

gcspopx.description: Discards an exception-return record from the guarded control stack, validating it first.

gcspushm.description: Pushes a register value onto the guarded control stack, which holds shadow return addresses.

gcspushx.description: Pushes an exception-return record onto the guarded control stack; used by exception entry code.

gcsss1.description: First half of switching to another guarded control stack: validates and pushes the stack-switch token.

gcsss2.description: Second half of a guarded control stack switch: finishes the switch and returns the old stack pointer.

gcsstr.description: Stores a register to memory using the guarded control stack permission rules, so it can write shadow stack pages.

gcssttr.description: Like GCSSTR but with unprivileged access checks, so kernels can write a user shadow stack on its behalf.

gic.description: Issues a Generic Interrupt Controller maintenance operation (such as cache or interrupt state management) chosen by the operand. Only meaningful in system software.

gicr.description: Runs a GIC operation that returns a result into a register. Used by interrupt-controller firmware or hypervisors.

gmi.description: Adds a tag value to an exclusion mask, so the IRG instruction avoids picking that memory tag. Part of memory tagging (MTE).

gsb.description: Barrier for GIC operations that waits until earlier GIC commands have taken effect.

hint.description: Generic encoding for hint instructions such as NOP, YIELD or WFE. Cores that do not understand a given number simply treat it as a no-op.

hlt.description: Triggers a debug halt event, used by debuggers and semihosting. Without a debugger attached it normally traps or is undefined.

hvc.description: Calls the hypervisor (EL2) from the guest OS (EL1), like a system call one level up.

ic.description: Invalidates instruction cache entries, for example by address, or the whole cache. Needed after writing code (JIT compilers).

ins.description: Copies a value into one lane of a vector, from a general register or another vector lane, leaving other lanes unchanged. MOV is an alias.

irg.description: Copies a pointer and puts a randomly chosen memory tag in its top bits, avoiding excluded tags. Used by MTE-aware allocators.

isb.description: Flushes the pipeline so later instructions are fetched afresh and see earlier system register or code changes. Used after self-modifying code or system register writes.

ld1.description: Loads one to four vector registers of consecutive memory, or a single lane. Elements are not de-interleaved.

ld1r.description: Loads one element from memory and copies it into every lane of a vector.

ld2.description: Loads interleaved pairs from memory and splits them across two registers, e.g. x in one and y in the other.

ld2r.description: Loads one 2-element structure and replicates each element across all lanes of two registers.

ld3.description: Loads interleaved triples (e.g. RGB pixels) and splits them across three registers.

ld3r.description: Loads one 3-element structure and replicates each element across all lanes of three registers.

ld4.description: Loads interleaved quadruples (e.g. RGBA pixels) and splits them across four registers.

ld4r.description: Loads one 4-element structure and replicates each element across all lanes of four registers.

ld64b.description: Loads 64 bytes from memory into eight consecutive general registers as a single atomic access. Meant for talking to accelerators.

ldadd.description: Atomically adds a register to a word or doubleword in memory (read-modify-write) and returns the original memory value in Xt/Wt. Memory ordering is relaxed. Used for atomic fetch_add in C/C++.

ldadda.description: Atomically adds a register to a word or doubleword in memory (read-modify-write) and returns the original memory value in Xt/Wt. Memory ordering is acquire. Used for atomic fetch_add in C/C++.

ldaddab.description: Atomically adds a register to a byte in memory (read-modify-write) and returns the original memory value in Xt/Wt. Memory ordering is acquire. Used for atomic fetch_add in C/C++.

ldaddah.description: Atomically adds a register to a halfword in memory (read-modify-write) and returns the original memory value in Xt/Wt. Memory ordering is acquire. Used for atomic fetch_add in C/C++.

ldaddal.description: Atomically adds a register to a word or doubleword in memory (read-modify-write) and returns the original memory value in Xt/Wt. Memory ordering is acquire-release. Used for atomic fetch_add in C/C++.

ldaddalb.description: Atomically adds a register to a byte in memory (read-modify-write) and returns the original memory value in Xt/Wt. Memory ordering is acquire-release. Used for atomic fetch_add in C/C++.

ldaddalh.description: Atomically adds a register to a halfword in memory (read-modify-write) and returns the original memory value in Xt/Wt. Memory ordering is acquire-release. Used for atomic fetch_add in C/C++.

ldaddb.description: Atomically adds a register to a byte in memory (read-modify-write) and returns the original memory value in Xt/Wt. Memory ordering is relaxed. Used for atomic fetch_add in C/C++.

ldaddh.description: Atomically adds a register to a halfword in memory (read-modify-write) and returns the original memory value in Xt/Wt. Memory ordering is relaxed. Used for atomic fetch_add in C/C++.

ldaddl.description: Atomically adds a register to a word or doubleword in memory (read-modify-write) and returns the original memory value in Xt/Wt. Memory ordering is release. Used for atomic fetch_add in C/C++.

ldaddlb.description: Atomically adds a register to a byte in memory (read-modify-write) and returns the original memory value in Xt/Wt. Memory ordering is release. Used for atomic fetch_add in C/C++.

ldaddlh.description: Atomically adds a register to a halfword in memory (read-modify-write) and returns the original memory value in Xt/Wt. Memory ordering is release. Used for atomic fetch_add in C/C++.

ldap.description: Loads two registers from memory with load-acquire (RCpc) ordering.

ldap1.description: Loads one 64-bit lane of a vector register with acquire (RCpc) ordering, leaving the other lane unchanged.

ldapp.description: Loads a register pair with RCpc acquire ordering, with a slightly weaker guarantee than LDAP, useful for lock-free queues.

ldapr.description: Loads a register with weaker-than-LDAR acquire semantics (RCpc). Used for C++ memory_order_acquire loads.

ldaprb.description: Loads a byte, zero-extended, with RCpc acquire ordering.

ldaprh.description: Loads a 16-bit value, zero-extended, with RCpc acquire ordering.

ldapur.description: Load-acquire (RCpc) with a small signed byte offset that need not be aligned to the access size.

ldapurb.description: Loads a byte with RCpc acquire ordering and a signed byte offset, zero-extending.

ldapurh.description: Loads a halfword with RCpc acquire ordering and a signed byte offset, zero-extending.

ldapursb.description: Loads a byte with RCpc acquire ordering and sign-extends it to 32 or 64 bits.

ldapursh.description: Loads a halfword with RCpc acquire ordering and sign-extends it.

ldapursw.description: Loads a 32-bit word with RCpc acquire ordering and sign-extends it to 64 bits.

ldar.description: Loads a register with acquire ordering: later memory accesses cannot be reordered before it. Used for atomic acquire loads and lock acquisition.

ldarb.description: Loads a byte, zero-extended, with acquire ordering.

ldarh.description: Loads a 16-bit value from memory and zero-extends it, with acquire ordering so later accesses cannot be moved before it. Used for acquire-loads of 16-bit atomics.

ldatxr.description: Exclusive load with acquire ordering that is performed with unprivileged access permissions. It is the load half of a lock-free read-modify-write loop, paired with a store-exclusive.

ldaxp.description: Loads two registers from consecutive memory and marks the address for exclusive monitoring, with acquire ordering. Pairs with STXP/STLXP for 128-bit atomic updates in older cores.

ldaxr.description: Loads a word or doubleword and marks the address for exclusive access, with acquire ordering. Starts the retry loop of spin locks and atomic updates, finished by a store-exclusive.

ldaxrb.description: Exclusive load of one byte, zero-extended, with acquire ordering. Used for byte-sized lock or flag updates in a load/store-exclusive loop.

ldaxrh.description: Exclusive load of a 16-bit value, zero-extended, with acquire ordering. Used for halfword atomic updates in a load/store-exclusive loop.

ldbfadd.description: Atomically adds the BFloat16 source to the memory value and returns the old memory value in the destination register.

ldbfadda.description: Atomically adds the BFloat16 source to the memory value and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Suffix A: acquire: later accesses cannot move before it.

ldbfaddal.description: Atomically adds the BFloat16 source to the memory value and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Suffix AL: both acquire and release ordering.

ldbfaddl.description: Atomically adds the BFloat16 source to the memory value and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Suffix L: release: earlier accesses cannot move after it.

ldbfmax.description: Atomically stores the larger BFloat16 value and returns the old memory value in the destination register.

ldbfmaxa.description: Atomically stores the larger BFloat16 value and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Suffix A: acquire: later accesses cannot move before it.

ldbfmaxal.description: Atomically stores the larger BFloat16 value and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Suffix AL: both acquire and release ordering.

ldbfmaxl.description: Atomically stores the larger BFloat16 value and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Suffix L: release: earlier accesses cannot move after it.

ldbfmaxnm.description: Atomically stores the larger BFloat16 value, preferring a number over a quiet NaN and returns the old memory value in the destination register.

ldbfmaxnma.description: Atomically stores the larger BFloat16 value, preferring a number over a quiet NaN and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Suffix A: acquire: later accesses cannot move before it.

ldbfmaxnmal.description: Atomically stores the larger BFloat16 value, preferring a number over a quiet NaN and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Suffix AL: both acquire and release ordering.

ldbfmaxnml.description: Atomically stores the larger BFloat16 value, preferring a number over a quiet NaN and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Suffix L: release: earlier accesses cannot move after it.

ldbfmin.description: Atomically stores the smaller BFloat16 value and returns the old memory value in the destination register.

ldbfmina.description: Atomically stores the smaller BFloat16 value and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Suffix A: acquire: later accesses cannot move before it.

ldbfminal.description: Atomically stores the smaller BFloat16 value and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Suffix AL: both acquire and release ordering.

ldbfminl.description: Atomically stores the smaller BFloat16 value and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Suffix L: release: earlier accesses cannot move after it.

ldbfminnm.description: Atomically stores the smaller BFloat16 value, preferring a number over a quiet NaN and returns the old memory value in the destination register.

ldbfminnma.description: Atomically stores the smaller BFloat16 value, preferring a number over a quiet NaN and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Suffix A: acquire: later accesses cannot move before it.

ldbfminnmal.description: Atomically stores the smaller BFloat16 value, preferring a number over a quiet NaN and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Suffix AL: both acquire and release ordering.

ldbfminnml.description: Atomically stores the smaller BFloat16 value, preferring a number over a quiet NaN and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Suffix L: release: earlier accesses cannot move after it.

ldclr.description: Atomically clears the bits set in the source register and returns the old memory value in the destination register.

ldclra.description: Atomically clears the bits set in the source register and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Suffix A: acquire: later accesses cannot move before it.

ldclrab.description: Atomically clears the bits set in the source register and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Operates on a byte. Suffix A: acquire: later accesses cannot move before it.

ldclrah.description: Atomically clears the bits set in the source register and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Operates on a halfword. Suffix A: acquire: later accesses cannot move before it.

ldclral.description: Atomically clears the bits set in the source register and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Suffix AL: both acquire and release ordering.

ldclralb.description: Atomically clears the bits set in the source register and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Operates on a byte. Suffix AL: both acquire and release ordering.

ldclralh.description: Atomically clears the bits set in the source register and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Operates on a halfword. Suffix AL: both acquire and release ordering.

ldclrb.description: Atomically clears the bits set in the source register and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Operates on a byte.

ldclrh.description: Atomically clears the bits set in the source register and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Operates on a halfword.

ldclrl.description: Atomically clears the bits set in the source register and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Suffix L: release: earlier accesses cannot move after it.

ldclrlb.description: Atomically clears the bits set in the source register and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Operates on a byte. Suffix L: release: earlier accesses cannot move after it.

ldclrlh.description: Atomically clears the bits set in the source register and returns the old memory value in the destination register. Operates on a halfword. Suffix L: release: earlier accesses cannot move after it.

ldurh.description: Loads a 16-bit value, zero-extended, from base plus a small signed byte offset. Emitted for negative or unaligned offsets.

ldursb.description: Loads one byte from base plus a small signed offset and sign-extends it into a W or X register.

ldursh.description: Loads a 16-bit value from base plus a small signed offset and sign-extends it into a W or X register.

ldursw.description: Loads a 32-bit value from base plus a small signed offset and sign-extends it to 64 bits.

ldxp.description: Loads two registers from memory and marks the address for exclusive monitoring, so a later STXP can store atomically if nothing intervened. Used in lock-free 128-bit updates.

ldxr.description: Loads a value from memory and arms the exclusive monitor, pairing with STXR to build atomic read-modify-write loops on cores without LSE atomics.

ldxrb.description: Exclusive load of a single byte (zero-extended) that arms the monitor for a following STXRB.

ldxrh.description: Exclusive load of a 16-bit value (zero-extended) that arms the monitor for a following STXRH.

lsl.description: Shifts a register left by an immediate or by a register amount, filling with zeros. Immediate form is an alias of UBFM; register form is an alias of LSLV. Equivalent to multiplying by a power of two.

lslv.description: Shifts a register left by the amount in another register (taken modulo the register width), filling with zeros. LSL with a register operand is an alias of this.

lsr.description: Shifts a register right by an immediate or register amount, filling with zeros. Used for unsigned division by powers of two and field extraction. An alias of UBFM or LSRV.

lsrv.description: Shifts a register right by the amount in another register (modulo width), inserting zeros at the top. LSR with a register operand is an alias of this.

luti2.description: Uses 2-bit indices packed in a vector to pick elements out of a small table held in vector registers, producing a vector of the looked-up values. Useful for quantized data decoding.

luti4.description: Uses 4-bit indices packed in a vector to select elements from a table held in vector registers. Handy for decoding 4-bit quantized weights.

madd.description: Multiplies two registers and adds a third, all in one instruction. Compilers emit it for a*b+c; with a zero addend it is the MUL alias.

maddpt.description: Multiply-add variant from the checked-pointer arithmetic extension (FEAT_CPA) that treats operands as pointers and leaves the pointer's tag bits alone. Used for array index scaling.

mla.description: Multiplies matching elements of two vectors and adds the products to the destination elements. Used in dot-product style loops and filters.

mlbi.description: System instruction alias that invalidates cached MPAM (memory partitioning and monitoring) configuration entries in the lookaside buffers. Only used by privileged firmware or hypervisors.

mls.description: Multiplies matching vector elements and subtracts the products from the destination elements.

mneg.description: Multiplies two registers and negates the result. An alias of MSUB with the zero register as addend.

mov.description: Copies a register or loads a constant into a register. It is an alias that assembles to ORR, ADD, MOVZ, MOVN, or a vector/SVE copy depending on operands.

movi.description: Fills every element of a vector register with a constant, or builds a 64-bit mask-style constant. Used to zero vectors or create masks.

movk.description: Replaces one 16-bit chunk of a register with an immediate, leaving other bits unchanged. Used after MOVZ/MOVN to build large constants piece by piece.

movn.description: Loads a 16-bit immediate shifted into position and inverts the whole value, so constants like -1 or 0xFFFF0000... can be made in one instruction.

movz.description: Loads a 16-bit immediate at a chosen 16-bit position and zeros the rest of the register. The standard first step in building a constant.

mrrs.summary: Move system register pair to registers
mrrs.description: Reads a 128-bit system register into two consecutive general registers. Used by privileged code on cores with 128-bit system registers (FEAT_SYSREG128).

mrs.description: Reads a system register (such as TPIDR_EL0, NZCV or CNTVCT_EL0) into a general register. Used for thread pointers, timers, and CPU feature queries.

msr.description: Writes a general register or immediate to a system register or PSTATE field. Used by kernels, and by user code for TPIDR_EL0, FPCR, and NZCV.

msrr.summary: Move register pair to system register
msrr.description: Writes two consecutive general registers to a 128-bit system register (FEAT_SYSREG128).

msub.description: Multiplies two registers and subtracts the product from a third. Emitted for c-a*b and remainder calculations after a divide; MNEG is the zero-addend alias.

msubpt.description: Multiply-subtract from the checked-pointer arithmetic extension (FEAT_CPA); computes pointer minus scaled index while preserving tag bits.

mul.description: Multiplies two values and keeps the low half of the result. Scalar form is an alias of MADD with a zero addend; the vector form multiplies element by element.

mvn.description: Inverts every bit of a register (optionally after shifting). Alias of ORN with the zero register; the vector form inverts each element.

mvni.description: Fills vector elements with the bitwise inverse of an immediate constant. Useful for building masks like 0xFFFFFF00.

neg.description: Computes the two's-complement negative of a value. Alias of SUB from zero for scalars; the vector form negates each element.

negs.description: Negates a value and updates the condition flags, as if comparing zero with the operand. Alias of SUBS from the zero register.

ngc.description: Computes the negative of a value minus the borrow from the carry flag. Used for multi-word negation. Alias of SBC from zero.

ngcs.description: Like NGC but also updates the flags. Used for the final word of multi-precision negation. Alias of SBCS from zero.

nop.description: Does nothing and just advances to the next instruction. Compilers and assemblers use it for alignment padding or patchable code sites.

not.description: Inverts every bit of a vector register. The assembler spelling of the vector form of MVN.

orn.description: ORs one register with the inverted bits of another (optionally shifted). Also the basis of MVN.

orr.description: ORs two registers or a register with a bitmask immediate. Also used (with the zero register) to implement MOV.

pacda.summary: Sign pointer with data key A
pacda.description: Adds a pointer authentication code to a data pointer using key A and a modifier register. Protects data pointers from tampering.

pacdb.summary: Sign pointer with data key B
pacdb.description: Adds an authentication code to a data pointer using key B and a modifier register.

pacdza.summary: Sign pointer with data key A (zero modifier)
pacdza.description: Signs a data pointer with key A using zero as the modifier.

pacdzb.summary: Sign pointer with data key B (zero modifier)
pacdzb.description: Signs a data pointer with key B using zero as the modifier.

pacga.description: Computes a 32-bit authentication code from two registers using the generic key and places it in the top half of the result. Used to sign arbitrary data.

pacia.summary: Sign pointer with instruction key A
pacia.description: Adds an authentication code to a code pointer using key A and a modifier register.

pacia1716.summary: Sign X17 with key A, modifier X16
pacia1716.description: Hint-space form that signs X17 using instruction key A and X16 as modifier. Used in PLT stubs and runtime code.

pacia171615.summary: Sign X17 with key A, modifier X15
pacia171615.description: Hint-space form signing X17 with instruction key A and X15 as modifier.

paciasp.summary: Sign LR with key A using SP
paciasp.description: Signs the link register with instruction key A using the stack pointer as modifier. Placed in function prologues for return-address protection.

paciasppc.summary: Sign LR with key A using SP and PC
paciasppc.description: Signs the link register with key A, mixing in both the stack pointer and the address of this instruction (FEAT_PAuth_LR).

paciaz.summary: Sign LR with key A, zero modifier
paciaz.description: Signs the link register with instruction key A using zero as the modifier.

pacib.summary: Sign pointer with instruction key B
pacib.description: Adds an authentication code to a code pointer using key B and a modifier register.

pacib1716.summary: Sign X17 with key B, modifier X16
pacib1716.description: Hint-space form that signs X17 using instruction key B with X16 as modifier.

pacib171615.summary: Sign X17 with key B, modifier X15
pacib171615.description: Hint-space form signing X17 with instruction key B and X15 as modifier.

pacibsp.summary: Sign LR with key B using SP
pacibsp.description: Signs the link register with instruction key B using the stack pointer as modifier. Common in function prologues on hardened builds.

pacibsppc.summary: Sign LR with key B using SP and PC
pacibsppc.description: Signs the link register with key B, mixing in the stack pointer and this instruction's address (FEAT_PAuth_LR).

pacibz.summary: Sign LR with key B, zero modifier
pacibz.description: Signs the link register with instruction key B using zero as the modifier.

paciza.summary: Sign pointer with key A, zero modifier
paciza.description: Signs a code pointer with instruction key A and a zero modifier.

pacizb.summary: Sign pointer with key B, zero modifier
pacizb.description: Signs a code pointer with instruction key B and a zero modifier.

pacm.description: Hint-space instruction that combines the PC-derived value into the modifier used by the PAuth_LR signing and authenticating instructions (FEAT_PAuth_LR).

pacnbiasppc.summary: Sign LR key A, SP and PC, non-bit-preserving
pacnbiasppc.description: Like PACIASPPC, but the signature replaces upper bits without preserving a bit, FEAT_PAuth_LR variant.

pacnbibsppc.summary: Sign LR key B, SP and PC, non-bit-preserving
pacnbibsppc.description: Like PACIBSPPC, but the signature replaces upper bits without preserving a bit, FEAT_PAuth_LR variant.

pmul.description: Multiplies byte elements as polynomials over GF(2) (carry-less) and keeps the low 8 bits. Used in CRC and Galois-field math.

pmull.description: Carry-less multiplies elements from the lower half of the sources into double-width results. The 64-bit form (PMULL.1Q) is key to fast CRC and GCM.

pmull2.description: Like PMULL but reads the upper halves of the source vectors.

prfm.description: Hints that an address will soon be read or written so the cache can fetch it early. Has no architectural effect on results.

prfum.description: Prefetch hint using a small signed byte offset that need not be aligned. Does not change program results.

psb.description: Ensures that all earlier samples from the statistical profiling unit are written to the buffer before later instructions proceed.

pssbb.description: Prevents later loads from speculatively bypassing earlier stores to the same physical address. A mitigation against speculative-store-bypass attacks.

raddhn.summary: Add, round, narrow to high half
raddhn.description: Adds two vectors of wide elements, rounds, and keeps only the top half of each sum in a narrower element. Used in fixed-point scaling.

raddhn2.description: Like RADDHN but writes the narrowed results into the upper half of the destination, preserving the lower half.

rax1.description: Rotates each 64-bit element of one vector left by 1 and XORs it with the other. Part of the SHA-3 acceleration instructions.

rbit.description: Reverses the order of all bits in a register. Combined with CLZ to count trailing zeros, or for bit-reversed addressing.

ret.description: Jumps to the address in a register, by default X30 (the link register), ending the current function. Hints to the CPU that this is a return so it predicts it using the return stack.

retaa.description: Authenticates the return address in X30 using key A and SP as the modifier, then returns. Compilers emit it in functions protected by pointer-authentication return signing.

retaasppc.description: Returns after authenticating a link address that was signed with the PC value of the signing site (PACIASPPC), using key A. Part of the PAuth_LR extension.

retaasppcr.summary: Return with PC-authentication from register (key A)
retaasppcr.description: Like RETAASPPC but takes the link address from a general register instead of X30. Part of the PAuth_LR extension.

retab.description: Authenticates the return address in X30 using key B and SP as the modifier, then returns. Used in functions that sign their return address with PACIBSP.

retabsppc.description: Returns after authenticating a link address that was signed with the PC value of the signing site, using key B. Part of the PAuth_LR extension.

retabsppcr.summary: Return with PC-authentication from register (key B)
retabsppcr.description: Like RETABSPPC but takes the link address from a general register instead of X30. Part of the PAuth_LR extension.

rev.description: Reverses the order of all bytes in a register, converting between big-endian and little-endian. Compilers use it for byte-swap intrinsics and network-order conversions.

rev16.description: Swaps the two bytes within each 16-bit halfword of the register independently.
rev16.operation: Xd = bswap16 of each halfword of Xn

rev32.description: Reverses the bytes inside each 32-bit word of a 64-bit register independently.
rev32.operation: Xd = bswap32 of each word of Xn

rev64.description: Reverses the order of the narrower elements inside each 64-bit chunk of a SIMD vector (or the bytes of a general register, as an alias of REV).
rev64.operation: Vd = reverse elements in each 64-bit lane of Vn

rmif.description: Rotates a register right by an amount, then copies selected bits of the result into the NZCV flags according to a mask. Helps emulate flag behaviour of other architectures.

ror.description: Rotates the bits of a register right, with bits falling off the bottom re-entering at the top. An alias of EXTR (immediate amount) or RORV (register amount).

rorv.description: Rotates a register right by an amount held in another register (taken modulo the register width). ROR with a register operand is an alias of this.

rprfm.description: Hints that a range of memory described by a register will be accessed soon, so the CPU may bring it into cache. It never faults and does not change program results.
rprfm.operation: prefetch range described by Xt at [Xn]

rshrn.description: Shifts each element right by an immediate with rounding, then narrows the result to half the width, writing the lower half of the destination.

rshrn2.description: Same as RSHRN but writes the narrowed results into the upper half of the destination vector, leaving the lower half unchanged.

rsubhn.description: Subtracts elements, rounds, and keeps only the top half of each difference, producing narrower elements in the lower half of the destination.

rsubhn2.description: Like RSUBHN but stores the narrowed results in the upper half of the destination vector.

saba.description: For each element, computes the absolute difference of two signed values and adds it to the destination. Common in motion-estimation and image kernels.

sabal.description: Takes absolute differences of the lower-half signed elements, widens them, and accumulates into the destination.

sabal2.description: Like SABAL but reads the upper halves of the source vectors.

sabd.description: Computes the absolute difference between corresponding signed elements of two vectors.

sabdl.description: Absolute difference of signed elements from the lower halves of the sources, stored at double width.

sabdl2.description: Like SABDL but uses the upper halves of the source vectors.

sadalp.summary: Signed add pairwise and accumulate long
sadalp.description: Adds adjacent pairs of signed elements, widens the sums, and accumulates them into the destination elements.

saddl.description: Adds signed elements from the lower halves of two vectors, producing double-width results.

saddl2.description: Like SADDL but works on the upper halves of the source vectors.

saddlp.description: Adds adjacent pairs of signed elements and stores each sum at double width.

saddlv.description: Sums all signed elements of a vector into one scalar with a wider type.

saddw.description: Adds the signed lower-half elements of a narrow vector to the elements of a wide vector.

saddw2.description: Like SADDW but takes the narrow operand from the upper half of the source.

sb.description: Stops the CPU speculatively executing later instructions until earlier ones have completed. Used to mitigate Spectre-style speculative side channels.

sbc.description: Subtracts a register and the inverted carry flag (the borrow) from another register. Used for multi-word subtraction after SUBS.

sbcs.description: Like SBC but also updates NZCV from the result. Used in multi-precision subtraction chains and comparisons.

sbfiz.description: Takes the low bits of a register, sign-extends them, and places them at a chosen bit position in an otherwise zero result. An alias of SBFM; emitted for shift-and-sign-extend.

sbfm.description: General bitfield extractor or inserter that sign-extends the result. ASR, SXTB, SXTH, SXTW, SBFX and SBFIZ are aliases of it.

sbfx.description: Extracts a run of bits from a register and sign-extends it to the full width. An alias of SBFM, used for signed struct bitfield reads.

scvtf.description: Converts a signed integer, from a general or SIMD register, to a floating-point value, optionally dividing by a power of two for fixed-point input.

sdiv.description: Divides one signed integer by another, rounding toward zero. Division by zero gives 0 rather than trapping.

sdot.description: Multiplies groups of four signed bytes and sums the products into 32-bit accumulators. Used heavily in quantised neural-network code.

setf8.description: Sets N, Z and V flags as if an 8-bit operation had produced the low byte of the register. Used to emulate narrow arithmetic flags.
