setmn.description: Performs the bulk of a memset operation; the three-instruction P, M, E sequence together implements a memset. This is the non-temporal variant. Emitted by compilers or libc for memset-like loops (FEAT_MOPS).

setmt.description: Performs the bulk of a memset operation; the three-instruction P, M, E sequence together implements a memset. This is the unprivileged variant. Emitted by compilers or libc for memset-like loops (FEAT_MOPS).

setmtn.description: Performs the bulk of a memset operation; the three-instruction P, M, E sequence together implements a memset. This is the unprivileged non-temporal variant. Emitted by compilers or libc for memset-like loops (FEAT_MOPS).

setp.description: Starts a memset operation, preparing the size and pointers and possibly doing part of the work; the three-instruction P, M, E sequence together implements a memset. Emitted by compilers or libc for memset-like loops (FEAT_MOPS).

setpn.description: Starts a memset operation, preparing the size and pointers and possibly doing part of the work; the three-instruction P, M, E sequence together implements a memset. This is the non-temporal variant. Emitted by compilers or libc for memset-like loops (FEAT_MOPS).

setpt.description: Starts a memset operation, preparing the size and pointers and possibly doing part of the work; the three-instruction P, M, E sequence together implements a memset. This is the unprivileged variant. Emitted by compilers or libc for memset-like loops (FEAT_MOPS).

setptn.description: Starts a memset operation, preparing the size and pointers and possibly doing part of the work; the three-instruction P, M, E sequence together implements a memset. This is the unprivileged non-temporal variant. Emitted by compilers or libc for memset-like loops (FEAT_MOPS).

sev.description: Hint that wakes all cores waiting in WFE by setting their event register. Used in spinlock release code.

sevl.description: Hint that sets the event register of only the current core, so its next WFE returns immediately. Used to prime wait loops.

sha1c.description: Performs four rounds of SHA-1 using the choose function. Part of the crypto extension.

sha1h.description: Rotates a 32-bit value left by 30, a step of the SHA-1 schedule.

sha1m.description: Performs four rounds of SHA-1 using the majority function.

sha1p.description: Performs four rounds of SHA-1 using the parity function.

sha1su0.description: First half of computing the next four SHA-1 message schedule words.

sha1su1.description: Second half of computing four SHA-1 message schedule words.

sha256h.description: Performs four SHA-256 rounds and produces the updated first half of the hash state.

sha256h2.description: Performs four SHA-256 rounds and produces the updated second half of the hash state.

sha256su0.description: First step of generating SHA-256 message schedule words.

sha256su1.description: Second step of generating SHA-256 message schedule words.

sha512h.description: Performs part of a SHA-512 round computation on 64-bit state words.

sha512h2.description: Performs the second part of a SHA-512 round computation.

sha512su0.description: First step of SHA-512 message schedule update.

sha512su1.description: Second step of SHA-512 message schedule update.

shadd.description: Adds signed elements and shifts the sum right by one, giving an overflow-free average that truncates.

shl.description: Shifts every vector element left by a constant, filling with zeros.

shll.description: Widens each lower-half element to double width and shifts it left by the element size.

shll2.description: Like SHLL but takes elements from the upper half of the source vector.

shrn.description: Shifts each element right by a constant and narrows it to half width, writing the lower half of the destination.

shrn2.description: Like SHRN but writes the narrowed results to the upper half of the destination.

shsub.description: Subtracts signed elements and halves the result, without overflow.

shuh.description: A hint telling the CPU that the data being accessed is likely shared with other cores, so it can tune cache handling. It has no architectural effect on results.

sli.description: Shifts each element left and inserts it into the destination, keeping the destination bits below the shift amount unchanged.

sm3partw1.description: First step of SM3 hash message-word expansion (Chinese standard).

sm3partw2.description: Second step of SM3 message-word expansion.

sm3ss1.description: Computes the SS1 intermediate value used in SM3 compression rounds.

sm3tt1a.description: Computes the TT1 update for SM3 rounds in the first sixteen rounds.

sm3tt1b.description: Computes the TT1 update for later SM3 rounds.

sm3tt2a.description: Computes the TT2 update for SM3 rounds in the first sixteen rounds.

sm3tt2b.description: Computes the TT2 update for later SM3 rounds.

sm4e.description: Performs four rounds of SM4 block cipher encryption.

sm4ekey.description: Generates four SM4 round keys from the previous ones.

smaddl.description: Multiplies two signed 32-bit values to a 64-bit product and adds a 64-bit register.

smax.description: Picks the larger of two signed values, per element for vectors, or for general registers (FEAT_CSSC).

smaxp.description: Takes the maximum of adjacent signed element pairs across the concatenated sources.

smaxv.description: Finds the largest signed element in a vector.

smc.description: Traps to EL3 firmware, typically used by the OS or hypervisor to request secure-world services such as PSCI.

smin.description: Picks the smaller of two signed values, per element for vectors, or for general registers (FEAT_CSSC).

sminp.description: Takes the minimum of adjacent signed element pairs across the concatenated sources.

sminv.description: Finds the smallest signed element in a vector.

smlal.description: Multiplies signed lower-half elements, widens the products, and adds them to the destination.

smlal2.description: Like SMLAL but uses the upper halves of the sources.

smlsl.description: Multiplies signed lower-half elements and subtracts the widened products from the destination.

smlsl2.description: Like SMLSL but uses the upper halves of the sources.

smmla.description: Multiplies a 2x8 by an 8x2 signed byte matrix and accumulates into a 2x2 matrix of 32-bit values.

smnegl.description: Multiplies two signed 32-bit values and negates the 64-bit product. An alias of SMSUBL with XZR as the addend.

smov.summary: Signed move vector element to general
smov.description: Copies one vector element to a general register, sign-extending it.

smstart.description: Enters SME streaming SVE mode, enables the ZA array, or both, zeroing the affected state. An alias of an MSR to SVCR.

smstop.description: Leaves SME streaming SVE mode, disables ZA, or both, discarding the affected state. An alias of an MSR to SVCR.

smsubl.description: Multiplies two signed 32-bit values and subtracts the 64-bit product from a 64-bit register.

smulh.description: Computes the 128-bit signed product of two 64-bit registers and returns the upper 64 bits.

smull.description: Multiplies signed elements from lower halves into wider products. The general-register form multiplies two 32-bit values into a 64-bit result, an alias of SMADDL.

smull2.description: Like SMULL but uses the upper halves of the source vectors.

sqabs.description: Takes the absolute value of each element, clamping the most-negative value to the maximum.

sqadd.description: Adds signed elements, clamping at the type limits instead of wrapping.

sqdmlal.description: Multiplies lower-half signed elements, doubles the product with saturation, and accumulates with saturation.

sqdmlal2.description: Like SQDMLAL but reads the upper halves of the sources.

sqdmlsl.description: Multiplies lower-half signed elements, doubles the product, and subtracts it from the destination with saturation.

sqdmlsl2.description: Like SQDMLSL but reads the upper halves of the sources.

sqdmulh.description: Multiplies signed elements, doubles the product, and keeps the upper half, saturating on overflow. Used for fixed-point (Q15/Q31) math.

sqdmull.description: Multiplies lower-half signed elements and doubles the widened product with saturation.

sqdmull2.description: Like SQDMULL but uses the upper halves of the sources.

sqneg.description: Negates each element, clamping the most-negative value to the maximum.

sqrdmlah.summary: Saturating rounding doubling multiply accumulate high
sqrdmlah.description: Multiplies elements pairwise, doubles and rounds the product, keeps the high half and adds it to the destination with saturation. Used in fixed-point DSP code.

sqrdmlsh.summary: Saturating rounding doubling multiply subtract high
sqrdmlsh.description: Like SQRDMLAH but the rounded high half of the doubled product is subtracted from the destination, with saturation.

sqrdmulh.description: Multiplies elements, doubles the product, rounds and keeps the high half, saturating on overflow. Common for Q15/Q31 fixed-point math.

sqrshl.description: Shifts each signed element by a signed per-element amount from a register (negative shifts right with rounding), saturating on overflow.

sqrshrn.description: Shifts each signed element right by an immediate with rounding, then narrows to half width with signed saturation.

sqrshrn2.description: Same as SQRSHRN but writes the narrowed results into the upper half of the destination, leaving the lower half unchanged.

sqrshrun.summary: Saturating rounding shift right unsigned narrow
sqrshrun.description: Shifts signed elements right with rounding and narrows to an unsigned result, clamping negatives to zero and overflow to the maximum.

sqrshrun2.summary: Saturating rounding shift right unsigned narrow (upper)
sqrshrun2.description: Like SQRSHRUN but the narrowed results go into the upper half of the destination vector; the lower half is preserved.

sqshl.description: Shifts signed elements left by an immediate or by per-element register amounts, saturating on overflow instead of wrapping.

sqshlu.description: Shifts signed elements left by an immediate and saturates the result to an unsigned range, so negatives become zero.

sqshrn.description: Shifts signed elements right by an immediate and narrows to half width with signed saturation (no rounding).

sqshrn2.description: Like SQSHRN but writes the narrowed results into the upper half of the destination, keeping the lower half.

sqshrun.description: Shifts signed elements right and narrows to unsigned, clamping to the unsigned range of the smaller type.

sqshrun2.description: Like SQSHRUN but results are placed in the upper half of the destination vector.

sqsub.description: Subtracts signed elements and clamps to the representable range rather than wrapping around.

sqxtn.description: Narrows each signed element to half width, clamping values that do not fit.

sqxtn2.description: Like SQXTN but writes the narrowed elements into the upper half of the destination, preserving the lower half.

sqxtun.description: Narrows signed elements to an unsigned half-width value, clamping negatives to zero and large values to the maximum.

sqxtun2.description: Like SQXTUN but results fill the upper half of the destination vector.

srhadd.description: Adds signed elements with a rounding bit and shifts right by one, giving the rounded average without overflow.

sri.description: Shifts each element right and inserts it into the destination, keeping the top bits of the destination that the shift vacated.

srshl.description: Shifts signed elements by per-element signed amounts, rounding when the shift is rightward. No saturation.

srshr.description: Arithmetic right shift of each element by an immediate, with rounding.

srsra.summary: Signed rounding shift right and accumulate
srsra.description: Rounds and arithmetic-shifts elements right, then adds the result to the destination.

ssbb.description: Barrier that stops later loads from speculatively reading stale data past earlier stores to the same address. A mitigation for speculative store bypass attacks; alias of DSB #0.

sshl.description: Shifts signed elements left by per-element signed amounts; negative amounts shift right arithmetically.

sshll.description: Sign-extends each element of the lower half to double width and shifts it left by an immediate. Also the SXTL alias when shift is 0.

sshll2.description: Like SSHLL but reads the upper half of the source vector.

sshr.description: Arithmetic right shift of each vector element by an immediate.

ssra.description: Arithmetic-shifts elements right and adds them to the destination.

ssubl.description: Subtracts sign-extended elements from the lower halves of two vectors, producing double-width results.

ssubl2.description: Like SSUBL but uses the upper halves of the source vectors.

ssubw.description: Subtracts sign-extended elements of the lower half of the second vector from a double-width first vector.

ssubw2.description: Like SSUBW but reads the upper half of the narrow source vector.

st1.description: Stores one to four vector registers (or a single lane) to consecutive memory, with no interleaving. Used for plain vector stores and lane stores.

st2.description: Stores two vectors interleaved element by element (x0,y0,x1,y1...), e.g. packing separate channels into pairs.

st2g.description: Memory tagging: writes the allocation tag from a register to two consecutive 16-byte granules and stores nothing else.

st3.description: Stores three vectors interleaved element by element, such as writing planar R,G,B data as packed pixels.

st4.description: Stores four vectors interleaved element by element, e.g. packing RGBA planes into pixels.

st64b.description: Single-copy atomic 64-byte store from eight consecutive registers, used for accelerator or device submission queues.

st64bv.description: Atomic 64-byte store that returns a status in a register telling whether the device accepted it.

st64bv0.description: Like ST64BV but also supplies the ACCDATA_EL1 value with the store; used for accelerator work submission.

stadd.description: Atomically adds a register value into a word or doubleword in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDADD with the result sent to the zero register.

staddb.description: Atomically adds a register value into a byte in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDADDB with the result sent to the zero register.

staddh.description: Atomically adds a register value into a halfword in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDADDH with the result sent to the zero register.

staddl.description: Atomically adds a register value into a word or doubleword in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDADDL with the result sent to the zero register.

staddlb.description: Atomically adds a register value into a byte in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDADDLB with the result sent to the zero register.

staddlh.description: Atomically adds a register value into a halfword in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDADDLH with the result sent to the zero register.

stbfadd.description: Atomically combines a BFloat16 register value with memory (add), discarding the old value. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stbfaddl.description: Atomically combines a BFloat16 register value with memory (add), discarding the old value, with release ordering. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stbfmax.description: Atomically combines a BFloat16 register value with memory (maximum), discarding the old value. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stbfmaxl.description: Atomically combines a BFloat16 register value with memory (maximum), discarding the old value, with release ordering. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stbfmaxnm.description: Atomically combines a BFloat16 register value with memory (maxNum), discarding the old value. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stbfmaxnml.description: Atomically combines a BFloat16 register value with memory (maxNum), discarding the old value, with release ordering. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stbfmin.description: Atomically combines a BFloat16 register value with memory (minimum), discarding the old value. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stbfminl.description: Atomically combines a BFloat16 register value with memory (minimum), discarding the old value, with release ordering. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stbfminnm.description: Atomically combines a BFloat16 register value with memory (minNum), discarding the old value. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stbfminnml.description: Atomically combines a BFloat16 register value with memory (minNum), discarding the old value, with release ordering. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stclr.description: Atomically bit-clears a register value into a word or doubleword in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDCLR with the result sent to the zero register.

stclrb.description: Atomically bit-clears a register value into a byte in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDCLRB with the result sent to the zero register.

stclrh.description: Atomically bit-clears a register value into a halfword in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDCLRH with the result sent to the zero register.

stclrl.description: Atomically bit-clears a register value into a word or doubleword in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDCLRL with the result sent to the zero register.

stclrlb.description: Atomically bit-clears a register value into a byte in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDCLRLB with the result sent to the zero register.

stclrlh.description: Atomically bit-clears a register value into a halfword in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDCLRLH with the result sent to the zero register.

stcph.description: A hint that the next store (or atomic) should be ordered ahead of other threads' accesses to the same location when contended. Executes as a no-op on cores without support.

steor.description: Atomically XORs a register value into a word or doubleword in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDEOR with the result sent to the zero register.

steorb.description: Atomically XORs a register value into a byte in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDEORB with the result sent to the zero register.

steorh.description: Atomically XORs a register value into a halfword in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDEORH with the result sent to the zero register.

steorl.description: Atomically XORs a register value into a word or doubleword in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDEORL with the result sent to the zero register.

steorlb.description: Atomically XORs a register value into a byte in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDEORLB with the result sent to the zero register.

steorlh.description: Atomically XORs a register value into a halfword in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDEORLH with the result sent to the zero register.

stfadd.description: Atomically combines a floating-point register value with memory (add), discarding the old value. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stfaddl.description: Atomically combines a floating-point register value with memory (add), discarding the old value, with release ordering. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stfmax.description: Atomically combines a floating-point register value with memory (maximum), discarding the old value. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stfmaxl.description: Atomically combines a floating-point register value with memory (maximum), discarding the old value, with release ordering. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stfmaxnm.description: Atomically combines a floating-point register value with memory (maxNum), discarding the old value. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stfmaxnml.description: Atomically combines a floating-point register value with memory (maxNum), discarding the old value, with release ordering. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stfmin.description: Atomically combines a floating-point register value with memory (minimum), discarding the old value. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stfminl.description: Atomically combines a floating-point register value with memory (minimum), discarding the old value, with release ordering. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stfminnm.description: Atomically combines a floating-point register value with memory (minNum), discarding the old value. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stfminnml.description: Atomically combines a floating-point register value with memory (minNum), discarding the old value, with release ordering. Alias of the matching load form with the result discarded.

stg.description: Memory tagging (MTE): sets the allocation tag of one 16-byte granule to the tag in the register.

stgm.description: Memory tagging: stores a block of allocation tags from a register to the tag memory for a region (privileged).

stgp.description: Stores a pair of registers (16 bytes) and sets that granule's allocation tag from the base address.

stilp.description: Stores a register pair with release-consistent (RCpc) ordering, writing both values to consecutive memory.

stl1.description: Stores a single vector lane to memory with release ordering (RCpc SIMD extension).

stllr.description: Store with LORegion release semantics (limited ordering regions).

stllrb.description: Byte-sized store with LORegion release ordering.

stllrh.description: Halfword-sized store with LORegion release ordering.

stlp.description: Stores two registers to memory as a pair with release ordering.

stlr.description: Stores a register with release ordering: earlier accesses become visible first. Used for unlocking and atomic stores with release semantics.

stltxr.description: Exclusive store with release ordering (LORegion variant); reports success or failure in a status register.

stlur.description: Store-release using an unscaled signed 9-bit offset.

stlurb.description: Byte store-release with an unscaled signed offset.

stlurh.description: Halfword store-release with an unscaled signed offset.

stlxp.description: Exclusive store of two registers with release ordering; status register says whether it succeeded. Used in lock-free 128-bit updates.

stlxr.description: Exclusive store with release ordering; writes 0 to the status register on success, 1 on failure. Paired with LDAXR/LDXR in atomic loops.

stlxrb.description: Byte exclusive store with release ordering and a success status.

stlxrh.description: Halfword exclusive store with release ordering and a success status.

stnp.description: Stores two registers with a hint that the data will not be reused soon, so caches need not keep it.

stp.description: Stores two registers to adjacent memory locations in one instruction; ubiquitous in function prologues to save registers like x29/x30.

str.description: Writes a register to memory at base plus offset, with optional pre/post-index. The standard store.

strb.description: Writes the low byte of a register to memory.

strh.description: Writes the low 16 bits of a register to memory.

stset.description: Atomically ORs a register value into a word or doubleword in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDSET with the result sent to the zero register.

stsetb.description: Atomically ORs a register value into a byte in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDSETB with the result sent to the zero register.

stseth.description: Atomically ORs a register value into a halfword in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDSETH with the result sent to the zero register.

stsetl.description: Atomically ORs a register value into a word or doubleword in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDSETL with the result sent to the zero register.

stsetlb.description: Atomically ORs a register value into a byte in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDSETLB with the result sent to the zero register.

stsetlh.description: Atomically ORs a register value into a halfword in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDSETLH with the result sent to the zero register.

stshh.description: A hint that the following store targets data other threads are likely to read soon (KEEP or STRM cache policy), so it should propagate quickly. Harmless no-op where unsupported.

stsmax.description: Atomically takes signed max with a register value into a word or doubleword in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDSMAX with the result sent to the zero register.

stsmaxb.description: Atomically takes signed max with a register value into a byte in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDSMAXB with the result sent to the zero register.

stsmaxh.description: Atomically takes signed max with a register value into a halfword in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDSMAXH with the result sent to the zero register.

stsmaxl.description: Atomically takes signed max with a register value into a word or doubleword in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDSMAXL with the result sent to the zero register.

stsmaxlb.description: Atomically takes signed max with a register value into a byte in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDSMAXLB with the result sent to the zero register.

stsmaxlh.description: Atomically takes signed max with a register value into a halfword in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDSMAXLH with the result sent to the zero register.

stsmin.description: Atomically takes signed min with a register value into a word or doubleword in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDSMIN with the result sent to the zero register.

stsminb.description: Atomically takes signed min with a register value into a byte in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDSMINB with the result sent to the zero register.

stsminh.description: Atomically takes signed min with a register value into a halfword in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDSMINH with the result sent to the zero register.

stsminl.description: Atomically takes signed min with a register value into a word or doubleword in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDSMINL with the result sent to the zero register.

stsminlb.description: Atomically takes signed min with a register value into a byte in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDSMINLB with the result sent to the zero register.

stsminlh.description: Atomically takes signed min with a register value into a halfword in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDSMINLH with the result sent to the zero register.

sttadd.description: Atomically adds a register to memory using unprivileged access rules, discarding the old value. Alias of the LDT form.

sttaddl.description: Atomically adds a register to memory using unprivileged access rules with release ordering, discarding the old value. Alias of the LDT form.

sttclr.description: Atomically clears bits in memory using unprivileged access rules, discarding the old value. Alias of the LDT form.

sttclrl.description: Atomically clears bits in memory using unprivileged access rules with release ordering, discarding the old value. Alias of the LDT form.

sttnp.description: 128-bit-pair store with non-temporal hint, using unprivileged access.

sttp.description: Stores a register pair using unprivileged memory permissions.

sttr.description: Store that is checked as if executed at EL0, used by kernels writing to user memory.

sttrb.description: Byte store checked with EL0 permissions.

sttrh.description: Halfword store checked with EL0 permissions.

sttset.description: Atomically sets bits in memory using unprivileged access rules, discarding the old value. Alias of the LDT form.

sttsetl.description: Atomically sets bits in memory using unprivileged access rules with release ordering, discarding the old value. Alias of the LDT form.

sttxr.description: Exclusive store using unprivileged access, with a success status in a register.

stumax.description: Atomically takes unsigned max with a register value into a word or doubleword in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDUMAX with the result sent to the zero register.

stumaxb.description: Atomically takes unsigned max with a register value into a byte in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDUMAXB with the result sent to the zero register.

stumaxh.description: Atomically takes unsigned max with a register value into a halfword in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDUMAXH with the result sent to the zero register.

stumaxl.description: Atomically takes unsigned max with a register value into a word or doubleword in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDUMAXL with the result sent to the zero register.

stumaxlb.description: Atomically takes unsigned max with a register value into a byte in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDUMAXLB with the result sent to the zero register.

stumaxlh.description: Atomically takes unsigned max with a register value into a halfword in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDUMAXLH with the result sent to the zero register.

stumin.description: Atomically takes unsigned min with a register value into a word or doubleword in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDUMIN with the result sent to the zero register.

stuminb.description: Atomically takes unsigned min with a register value into a byte in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDUMINB with the result sent to the zero register.

stuminh.description: Atomically takes unsigned min with a register value into a halfword in memory, discarding the old value. An alias of LDUMINH with the result sent to the zero register.

stuminl.description: Atomically takes unsigned min with a register value into a word or doubleword in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDUMINL with the result sent to the zero register.

stuminlb.description: Atomically takes unsigned min with a register value into a byte in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDUMINLB with the result sent to the zero register.

stuminlh.description: Atomically takes unsigned min with a register value into a halfword in memory with release ordering, discarding the old value. An alias of LDUMINLH with the result sent to the zero register.

stur.description: Stores a register to memory using a signed 9-bit byte offset that need not be aligned to the access size. Used when the offset is negative or odd and the normal STR form cannot encode it.

sturb.description: Stores the low byte of a register to memory at base plus a small signed byte offset.

sturh.description: Stores the low 16 bits of a register to memory at base plus a small signed byte offset, with no alignment requirement from the offset encoding.

stxp.description: Tries to store two registers together as part of an exclusive (load-linked/store-conditional) sequence. A status register receives 0 on success or 1 if exclusivity was lost, so the code can retry.

stxr.description: The store half of a load-exclusive/store-exclusive pair. Writes the value only if nothing else touched the location since the matching LDXR, and reports 0 (success) or 1 (failed) in a status register.

stxrb.description: Conditional store of one byte, completing a LDXRB sequence. The status register gets 0 on success and 1 on failure.

stxrh.description: Conditional store of 16 bits, completing a LDXRH sequence. The status register gets 0 on success and 1 on failure.

stz2g.summary: Store zero to two tags and data
stz2g.description: Memory-tagging instruction that zeroes two 16-byte granules and sets their allocation tags from the tag in the address register. Used when allocators hand out tagged zeroed memory.

stzg.description: Memory-tagging instruction that zeroes one 16-byte granule and sets its allocation tag from the address's tag bits. Helps allocators clear and tag memory at once.

stzgm.description: Zeroes a block of tagged memory and writes allocation tags for it in one operation, with the block size defined by the CPU. Used for bulk clearing and tagging.
stzgm.operation: zero block at [Xn]; set tags from Xt

sub.description: Subtracts the second operand from the first and writes the result. The operand can be a register (optionally shifted or extended) or a small immediate. Also used for stack allocation like sub sp, sp, #16.

subg.description: Memory-tagging instruction that subtracts an immediate from an address and also changes its logical tag by a given amount. Used when moving pointers within tagged stack frames.

subhn.description: Subtracts two vectors of wide elements and keeps the upper half of each result, producing a vector of narrower elements in the low half of the destination.

subhn2.description: Like SUBHN but the narrowed results fill the upper half of the destination, leaving the lower half unchanged.

subp.description: Memory-tagging instruction that subtracts two pointers using only their 56-bit address parts, ignoring tag bits, and sign-extends the result.

subps.description: Same as SUBP (address-only pointer difference) but also updates the condition flags. CMPP is an alias of this with the result discarded.

subpt.description: Subtracts a register from a pointer in a way aimed at checked-pointer arithmetic, without altering the pointer's upper metadata in the usual way. Part of the newer pointer-arithmetic extension.

subs.description: Subtracts like SUB but also updates N, Z, C and V. CMP and NEGS are aliases of it; compilers use it directly for comparisons whose difference is also needed.

sudot.description: Multiplies groups of four signed 8-bit values by four unsigned 8-bit values and adds each group's sum into a 32-bit lane of the accumulator. Used in quantised int8 neural-network code.

suqadd.description: Adds an unsigned value to a signed element and clamps to the signed range instead of wrapping. Sets the sticky saturation flag if clamping occurred.

svc.description: Triggers a synchronous exception to enter the operating system kernel; it is how user programs make system calls. The 16-bit immediate is available to the handler.

swp.description: Atomically exchanges a register with a memory value, returning the old memory value. Used to implement atomic exchange and simple locks.

swpa.description: Atomic swap with acquire ordering: later memory accesses cannot be reordered before it.

swpab.description: Atomically exchanges a byte in memory with a register, with acquire ordering.

swpah.description: Atomically exchanges a 16-bit memory value with a register, with acquire ordering.

swpal.description: Atomic swap with both acquire and release ordering, giving full ordering around the exchange. Typical for sequentially consistent atomic exchange.

swpalb.description: Atomically exchanges a byte in memory with a register, with both acquire and release ordering.

swpalh.description: Atomically exchanges a 16-bit memory value with a register, with both acquire and release ordering.

swpb.description: Atomically exchanges a byte in memory with a register, with no ordering guarantees.

swph.description: Atomically exchanges a 16-bit memory value with a register, with no ordering guarantees.

swpl.description: Atomic swap with release ordering: earlier memory accesses complete before the exchange becomes visible. Used when releasing a lock.

swplb.description: Atomically exchanges a byte in memory with a register, with release ordering.

swplh.description: Atomically exchanges a 16-bit memory value with a register, with release ordering.

swpp.description: Atomically exchanges a 128-bit memory value with a pair of registers, returning the old value in another pair. Part of the 128-bit atomics extension.

swppa.description: 128-bit atomic swap using a register pair, with acquire ordering.

swppal.description: 128-bit atomic swap using a register pair, with acquire and release ordering.

swppl.description: 128-bit atomic swap using a register pair, with release ordering.

swpt.description: Atomic swap that is checked as if done by unprivileged code, even when executed from the kernel. Used by the OS to touch user memory safely.

swpta.description: Unprivileged-access atomic swap with acquire ordering.

swptal.description: Unprivileged-access atomic swap with acquire and release ordering.

swptl.description: Unprivileged-access atomic swap with release ordering.

sxtb.description: An alias of SBFM that takes the low 8 bits of a register and sign-extends them to 32 or 64 bits. Used when converting a signed char to a wider integer.

sxth.description: An alias of SBFM that sign-extends the low 16 bits of a register to 32 or 64 bits. Used for signed short to int/long conversion.

sxtl.description: An alias of SSHLL with a zero shift: widens each signed element in the lower half of a vector to double width.

sxtl2.description: An alias of SSHLL2 with zero shift: sign-extends each element in the upper half of the source vector to double width.

sxtw.description: An alias of SBFM that sign-extends the low 32 bits of a register to 64 bits. Common when using an int as an array index.

sys.description: Generic system instruction for cache, TLB and similar maintenance operations selected by op1, CRn, CRm, op2 fields. Aliases such as DC, IC, AT and TLBI are built on it.

sysl.description: Generic system instruction that returns a result into a general register. Used for implementation-defined or specialised system operations.

sysp.description: System instruction that takes a 128-bit register pair operand. TLBIP is an alias used for 128-bit TLB maintenance operations.

tbl.description: Uses bytes in the index vector to pick bytes from a table of one to four vector registers. Out-of-range indices give zero. Useful for byte shuffles and lookup tables.

tbnz.summary: Test bit and branch if nonzero
tbnz.description: Tests a single bit of a register and branches if it is 1. Compilers use it for sign-bit checks and single-flag tests.

tbx.description: Like TBL, but when an index is out of range the destination element keeps its old value instead of becoming zero.

tbz.summary: Test bit and branch if zero
tbz.description: Tests a single bit of a register and branches if it is 0. Common for checking boolean flags or sign bits without a separate compare.

tcancel.description: Part of the Transactional Memory Extension (TME), which Arm has since withdrawn: aborts the current transaction and rolls its effects back, passing a reason code to the code that started it. Apple processors never implemented it.

tchangeb.description: Part of FEAT_S1POE2 (the second Stage 1 Permission Overlay extension, 2025): the counterpart of TCHANGEF for the opposite direction, changing the TIndex that selects among permission overlays to the value of Xn or an immediate. No processor in phones or Macs implements it yet.

tchangef.description: Part of FEAT_S1POE2 (the second Stage 1 Permission Overlay extension, 2025): changes the TIndex, which selects among permission overlays, to the value of Xn or an immediate and returns a result in Xd. The F and B forms differ in direction. No processor in phones or Macs implements it yet.

tcommit.description: Part of the withdrawn Transactional Memory Extension (TME): ends the current transaction; when it is the outermost one, all its memory writes become visible to other processors at once.

tenter.description: Part of FEAT_TEV (TIndex exception-like vectors, a 2025 extension): enters a handler the way an exception would, through the vector entry the 7-bit immediate selects; TEXIT comes back. The optional nb is a variant the encoding allows. No processor in phones or Macs implements it yet.

texit.description: Part of FEAT_TEV (TIndex exception-like vectors, a 2025 extension): returns from a handler entered with TENTER, the way ERET returns from an exception.
texit.operation: return to the code that ran TENTER

tlbi.description: An alias of SYS that discards cached address-translation entries (by address, ASID, VMID, or all). Used by operating systems after changing page tables.

tlbip.description: An alias of SYSP that invalidates TLB entries using a 128-bit register-pair operand. Used by the OS after page-table changes with large addresses.

trcit.description: Writes a value to the trace unit as an instrumentation event, so profiling tools can see software markers. Does nothing if tracing is off.

trn1.description: Interleaves the even-numbered elements of two vectors, taking alternating ones from each. Used to build matrix transposes.

trn2.description: Interleaves the odd-numbered elements of two vectors, taking alternating ones from each. Pairs with TRN1 for transposition.

tsb.description: Hint that makes sure earlier trace data has been flushed to the trace buffer. Acts as a NOP when the feature is absent.

tst.description: An alias of ANDS that ANDs two values, sets flags and discards the result. Used to check whether certain bits are set, as in if (x & mask).

tstart.description: Part of the Transactional Memory Extension (TME), which Arm has since withdrawn: begins a transaction and sets Xt to 0. If the transaction fails, its effects are discarded and execution resumes after this instruction with the reason in Xt. Apple processors never implemented it.

ttest.description: Part of the withdrawn Transactional Memory Extension (TME): writes how deeply transactions are nested to Xt, 0 when no transaction is running.

uaba.description: For each element, computes the absolute difference between two unsigned values and adds it to the destination.

uabal.description: Takes absolute differences of unsigned elements from the lower halves of two vectors and adds them into double-width accumulator lanes.

uabal2.description: Like UABAL but works on the upper halves of the source vectors.

uabd.description: Computes the absolute difference between corresponding unsigned elements of two vectors. Handy in sum-of-absolute-differences image code.

uabdl.description: Absolute difference of unsigned elements from the lower halves of two vectors, giving double-width results.

uabdl2.description: Like UABDL but uses the upper halves of the source vectors.

uadalp.summary: Unsigned add pairwise and accumulate long
uadalp.description: Adds adjacent pairs of unsigned elements into double-width values and accumulates them into the destination.

uaddl.description: Adds elements from the lower halves of two vectors, zero-extending to double width so no overflow occurs.

uaddl2.description: Like UADDL but uses the upper halves of both source vectors.

uaddlp.description: Adds adjacent pairs of unsigned elements, producing half as many double-width elements.

uaddlv.description: Sums all elements of a vector into a single wider scalar. Used for horizontal sums of unsigned data.

uaddw.description: Adds the lower-half elements of a narrow vector, zero-extended, to the elements of a wide vector.

uaddw2.description: Like UADDW but takes the narrow operand from the upper half of the source vector.

ubfiz.description: An alias of UBFM that places the low bits of a register at a chosen position in a zeroed result. Compilers emit it for (x & mask) << n.

ubfm.description: General bitfield extract/insert with zero fill. LSL, LSR, UBFX, UBFIZ, UXTB and UXTH are aliases of it.
ubfm.operation: Xd = zero-extended bitfield move of Xn

ubfx.description: An alias of UBFM that pulls a run of bits out of a register and right-aligns it with zeros above. Equivalent to (x >> lsb) & mask.

ucvtf.description: Converts an unsigned integer (from a general register or SIMD register) to floating point, optionally treating it as fixed-point with fractional bits.

udf.description: Always raises an undefined-instruction exception. Compilers emit it for unreachable code or traps, and the 16-bit immediate can carry a code.

udiv.description: Divides one unsigned integer by another, rounding toward zero. Division by zero gives 0 rather than faulting.

udot.description: Multiplies groups of four unsigned 8-bit elements and adds each group's sum into a 32-bit accumulator lane. Used for int8 machine-learning kernels.

uhadd.description: Adds two unsigned elements and shifts the sum right by one, giving the average rounded down without overflow.

uhsub.description: Subtracts unsigned elements and halves the result, without intermediate overflow.

umaddl.description: Multiplies two 32-bit unsigned values into a 64-bit product and adds a 64-bit value. UMULL is its alias with zero addend.

umax.description: Picks the larger unsigned value from each pair of corresponding elements.

umaxp.description: Takes the maximum of each adjacent pair of unsigned elements across the concatenated inputs.
umaxp.operation: Vd = max of adjacent pairs of Vn:Vm

umaxv.description: Finds the largest unsigned element in a vector and puts it in a scalar result.

umin.description: Picks the smaller unsigned value from each pair of corresponding elements.

uminp.description: Takes the minimum of each adjacent pair of unsigned elements across the concatenated inputs.
uminp.operation: Vd = min of adjacent pairs of Vn:Vm

uminv.description: Finds the smallest unsigned element in a vector and puts it in a scalar result.

umlal.description: Multiplies unsigned elements from the lower halves of two vectors into double-width products and adds them to the destination.

umlal2.description: Like UMLAL but multiplies the upper halves of the source vectors.

umlsl.description: Multiplies unsigned elements from the lower halves into double-width products and subtracts them from the destination.

umlsl2.description: Like UMLSL but multiplies the upper halves of the source vectors.

ummla.description: Treats each source as a matrix of unsigned bytes (2x8 times 8x2) and adds the 2x2 product into 32-bit accumulators. Speeds up int8 matrix multiplication.

umnegl.description: An alias of UMSUBL with a zero accumulator: negates the 64-bit product of two unsigned 32-bit values.

umov.summary: Move vector element to general register
umov.description: Copies one element of a vector into a general register, zero-extending it. MOV is an alias for the 32/64-bit sizes.

umsubl.description: Multiplies two 32-bit unsigned values into a 64-bit product and subtracts it from a 64-bit value.

umulh.description: Multiplies two 64-bit unsigned values and returns the upper 64 bits of the 128-bit product. Used for wide multiplication and division by constants.

umull.description: Multiplies two 32-bit unsigned values into a 64-bit product (scalar alias of UMADDL), or SIMD lower-half elements into double-width products.

umull2.description: Multiplies unsigned elements from the upper halves of two vectors into double-width products.

uqadd.description: Adds unsigned elements and clamps to the maximum value instead of wrapping around. Sets the sticky saturation flag if clamping occurred.

uqrshl.description: Shifts each element by a signed per-element amount (negative shifts right) with rounding, clamping on overflow.

uqrshrn.summary: Unsigned saturating rounding shift right narrow
uqrshrn.description: Shifts right with rounding, then narrows each element to half width with clamping.

uqrshrn2.summary: Unsigned sat rounding shift right narrow (upper)
uqrshrn2.description: Like UQRSHRN but writes the narrowed results into the upper half of the destination.

uqshl.description: Shifts unsigned elements left by an immediate or per-element register amount, clamping to the maximum value on overflow.

uqshrn.description: Shifts right and narrows each element to half width, clamping values that do not fit.

uqshrn2.description: Like UQSHRN but writes the narrowed results into the upper half of the destination.

uqsub.description: Subtracts unsigned elements and clamps at zero instead of wrapping. Sets the saturation flag if clamping occurred.

uqxtn.description: Narrows each unsigned element to half width, clamping values too large to fit.

uqxtn2.description: Like UQXTN but writes the narrowed values into the upper half of the destination.

urecpe.description: Gives a rough fixed-point estimate of the reciprocal of each unsigned 32-bit element, as a starting point for refinement.

urhadd.description: Adds unsigned elements, adds one, and shifts right by one: the average rounded up. Common in image blending.

urshl.description: Shifts each element by a signed per-element amount (negative means right) with rounding.

urshr.description: Shifts unsigned elements right by an immediate, rounding to nearest instead of truncating.

ursqrte.description: Gives a rough estimate of the reciprocal square root of each unsigned 32-bit element for later refinement.

ursra.summary: Unsigned rounding shift right and accumulate
ursra.description: Shifts unsigned elements right by an immediate with rounding and adds the result to the destination.

usdot.description: Multiplies groups of four unsigned 8-bit values by four signed 8-bit values and adds each group's sum to a 32-bit accumulator lane.

ushl.description: Shifts each unsigned element by a signed per-element amount from another vector; negative amounts shift right.

ushll.description: Zero-extends lower-half elements to double width and shifts them left by an immediate. UXTL is its alias with zero shift.

ushll2.description: Like USHLL but takes elements from the upper half of the source vector.

ushr.description: Shifts each unsigned element right by an immediate, filling with zeros.

usmmla.description: Multiplies a 2x8 unsigned byte matrix by an 8x2 signed byte matrix and accumulates into a 2x2 matrix of 32-bit values.

usqadd.description: Adds a signed value to an unsigned element, clamping to the unsigned range. Sets the saturation flag on clamping.

usra.description: Shifts unsigned elements right by an immediate and adds the result to the destination.

usubl.description: Subtracts lower-half unsigned elements of two vectors, producing double-width results.

usubl2.description: Like USUBL but uses the upper halves of both source vectors.

usubw.description: Subtracts lower-half narrow unsigned elements, zero-extended, from the wide elements of another vector.

usubw2.description: Like USUBW but takes the narrow operand from the upper half of the source.

uxtb.description: An alias of UBFM that keeps the low 8 bits of a register and clears the rest. Used for unsigned char conversion.

uxth.description: An alias of UBFM that keeps the low 16 bits of a register and clears the rest. Used for unsigned short conversion.

uxtl.description: An alias of USHLL with zero shift: zero-extends each lower-half element to double width.

uxtl2.description: An alias of USHLL2 with zero shift: zero-extends each element in the upper half of the source to double width.

uzp1.description: Concatenates the even-numbered elements of two vectors, de-interleaving data such as split channels.

uzp2.description: Concatenates the odd-numbered elements of two vectors, de-interleaving data.

wfe.description: Hint that puts the core into a low-power state until an event occurs, such as a SEV from another core. Used in spinlock wait loops.

wfet.description: Like WFE but also wakes up when the system counter reaches a deadline held in a register.

wfi.description: Hint that puts the core into a low-power state until an interrupt or similar wake-up arrives. Used in idle loops.

wfit.description: Like WFI but also wakes when the system counter reaches the deadline in a register.

xaflag.summary: Convert float flags to alternative format
xaflag.description: Converts condition flags produced by a floating-point compare into the alternate encoding used by some other architectures' semantics. Rarely seen outside emulation.

xar.description: XORs two vectors and rotates each 64-bit element right by an immediate. Used in SHA-3 style hashing.

xpacd.description: Removes the pointer authentication signature from a data pointer, restoring the plain address.

xpaci.description: Removes the pointer authentication signature from a code pointer, restoring the plain address.

xpaclri.description: Removes the pointer authentication signature from the link register (X30). Runs as a NOP where pointer authentication is absent.

xtn.description: Truncates each element to half width, keeping the low half, and writes to the lower half of the destination.

xtn2.description: Like XTN but writes the narrowed elements into the upper half of the destination, keeping the lower half.

yield.description: Hint that tells the CPU this thread is spinning and other threads may run. Used in busy-wait loops on multithreaded cores.

zip1.description: Interleaves elements from the lower halves of two vectors, alternating between them.

zip2.description: Interleaves elements from the upper halves of two vectors, alternating between them.
